clues.description: Julian jokes about delivering pastries through three hotel service entrances after closing. Kitchen dispatch logs and the expired contract confirm the route and show that it ended before the disappearances.
clues.developerExplanation: He reveals the entrance knowledge as an ordinary chef story; the cross-check establishes when that work stopped.

lookingFor: A woman who enjoys food without turning dinner into a performance, can laugh during a kitchen mistake, and brings stories of her own to the table. I value reliability, honest apologies, and someone willing to stay for dessert even when the first course was imperfect.

name: Florian Metz
bio: Ask me about the painting, but be prepared for the longer answer.
description: Florian is thoughtful, articulate, and unable to answer a museum question briefly. Away from work he gardens, listens to history podcasts, and prefers plans that leave enough time to notice the room around him.

questions.question: Which forgotten story deserves retelling?
questions.answer: The hotel workers who knew every guest's secrets and still appear in history only as uniforms in the background.

questions.question: What makes someone a good storyteller?
questions.answer: Knowing which detail opens the door and which detail only proves that you did the research.

clues.description: Eleven months before the first disappearance, Florian recorded the line 'Your room is ready' for a public museum audio guide about a 1950s grand hotel. The recording remained freely available online.
clues.developerExplanation: The exact wording sounds private, but Florian's voice recording and transcript made the phrase public long before the crimes.

clues.description: Florian's museum biography credits him as narrator of the Grand Hotel exhibition. Its opening scene uses the same room-ready phrase later sent to the victims.
clues.developerExplanation: His profile creates a direct wording overlap, but the exhibition history shows that anyone could have heard and copied it.

clues.description: A folded transit ticket appears in Florian's exhibition photograph. It is a museum replica printed with a 1956 date and uses different paper from the minibar tickets.
clues.developerExplanation: The photograph combines hotel imagery and a folded ticket, but both are documented exhibition props.

clues.description: Florian quotes 'Your room is ready' while describing the museum exhibit he narrated. The public audio file and exhibition catalogue date the line eleven months before the first disappearance.
clues.developerExplanation: He repeats the suspicious phrase in a natural story; the cross-check shows that it was public material rather than private knowledge.

redHerrings: Audio guide was public for months
lookingFor: A woman who is patient with long stories but willing to interrupt with a better question. I admire quiet confidence, curiosity about the past, and anyone who can spend an afternoon in a museum before arguing cheerfully about where to eat.

name: Henrik Wolf
bio: I know the quickest route through any city, especially after midnight.
description: Henrik is composed, observant, and accustomed to making long journeys feel effortless. He says he now prefers local daytime driving, although older versions of his profile describe private overnight transfers and discreet hotel pickups.

questions.question: What makes a city feel familiar?
questions.answer: Knowing which roads remain quiet after midnight and which entrance saves five unnecessary minutes.

questions.question: What small habit follows you on every journey?
questions.answer: I keep paper tickets and fold them printed-side inward. Thermal ink disappears quickly if you leave it exposed.

clues.description: Henrik's driver login entered the hotel partner system seven to ten minutes before every false reservation was created. His phone then connected to the service lane at each hotel within three minutes of the 12:14 mobile-key entry.
clues.developerExplanation: The same driver account creates a preparation pattern before all three bookings, and Henrik's phone reaches each hidden pickup point at the critical time.

clues.description: Henrik now describes his work as local daytime driving. Archived versions of his profile repeatedly advertise discreet overnight transfers between Meridian House, Bell Tower Hotel, and Atlas Court.
clues.developerExplanation: His edited work description conceals the exact overnight hotel service needed to arrange and move every victim.

clues.description: A ticket corner in Henrik's car photograph carries the same current batch code and two inward folds found on every minibar ticket.
clues.developerExplanation: The batch and unusual folding pattern connect an object in Henrik's car directly to all three planted tickets.

clues.description: Henrik casually explains that he folds thermal tickets printed-side inward and names the locked side entrance used by each hotel after midnight. The minibar creases and access records match both details.
clues.developerExplanation: His ordinary dating chat reveals a distinctive folding habit and precise knowledge of all three hidden pickup points without him knowing why those details matter.

lookingFor: A woman who values privacy without confusing it with secrecy, enjoys quiet drives, and does not need every evening planned in advance. I am drawn to independence, dry humor, and someone who notices the city after everyone else has gone home.

name: Marco Stein
bio: If it has wheels, I probably have an opinion about its brakes.
description: Marco is cheerful, direct, and happiest with grease on his hands and a repair that finally runs quietly. He rides everywhere, gives unsolicited brake advice, and believes pizza is a valid reward for almost any distance.

questions.question: Which repair feels most satisfying?
questions.answer: A wheel that arrives wobbling and leaves silent. You can see the problem disappear one spoke at a time.

questions.question: What is your bad-weather plan?
questions.answer: Fix something indoors, order pizza, and pretend I never claimed rain makes cycling more interesting.

clues.description: Marco's ride tracker follows a midnight route past all three hotels. It belongs to a public Night Wheel event held two months before the first disappearance, and his account shows no hotel activity on the victim nights.
clues.developerExplanation: A large public bicycle ride explains the route. Its date and the absence of later activity separate Marco from the disappearances.

clues.description: Marco's profile celebrates the Night Wheel ride that passed Meridian House, Bell Tower Hotel, and Atlas Court. The event page and rider list confirm that hundreds followed the same route.
clues.developerExplanation: His route knowledge came from a public event rather than private travel between victim locations.

clues.description: A transit ticket tied to Marco's handlebar comes from the same batch as the minibar tickets. The transit authority distributed that batch to every Night Wheel participant two months earlier.
clues.developerExplanation: The batch match is genuine but not exclusive; hundreds of publicly distributed tickets provide the same possible source.

clues.description: Marco enthusiastically describes the Night Wheel route and the transit ticket tied to each rider's bike. Event records confirm the date, route, and mass distribution of the matching ticket batch.
clues.developerExplanation: He reveals the two suspicious details as a favorite cycling memory, and the cross-check shows that neither detail uniquely belongs to him.

redHerrings: Night ride passed all three hotels
lookingFor: A woman who makes decisions, apologizes properly, and can laugh when a shortcut becomes a long ride. She does not need to know anything about bicycles, but she should have a hobby that makes her forget to check the time.

name: Simon Adler
bio: I solve small emergencies before breakfast and remember everyone’s preferred tea.
description: Simon is observant, calm, and professionally trained to notice what a room needs before anyone asks. He manages a hotel, remembers regular guests' tea orders, and spends free days looking at architecture without checking the linen storage.

questions.question: What small kindness do you remember?
questions.answer: A night receptionist once saved me tea after a disastrous shift. It took thirty seconds and repaired the entire evening.

questions.question: What makes a room welcoming?
questions.answer: One comfortable chair, honest light, and a sign that a real person considered where you would put your coat.

clues.description: A regional audit account assigned to Simon opened records for all three hotels during the month of the disappearances. The account could review room preparation and entrances, but it could not create reservations or issue mobile keys.
clues.developerExplanation: Simon conducted legitimate quality audits across the hotel group. Read-only permissions prevent that account from producing any false check-in.

clues.description: Simon manages one hotel and occasionally performs regional overnight audits at the other two. His employer confirms the schedule and the restricted audit account.
clues.developerExplanation: His job gives him broad hotel knowledge, making him a strong red herring, but the verified role lacks the booking power used in the crimes.

clues.description: A map in Simon's profile photograph marks after-hours entrances at all three hotels. It belongs to a regional accessibility audit and carries the hotel group's approval stamp.
clues.developerExplanation: The map explains precise entrance knowledge while its project history and shared authorship keep it from becoming exclusive evidence.

clues.description: Simon naturally describes regional mystery audits and checking after-hours entrances. Employer records confirm the trips, while account permissions show that he could inspect bookings but not create them.
clues.developerExplanation: His dating chat makes him sound highly capable, but the separate permission check resolves the central reservation question.

redHerrings: Opened records at all three hotels
Audit account could not issue keys
lookingFor: A woman who is sincere without being careless, appreciates small kindnesses, and has a life that does not need managing. I like travel stories, strong tea, and people who can enjoy beautiful places without expecting every day to resemble a holiday.

name: Leon Bruck
bio: I find bugs for a living and still miss the obvious ones in my own kitchen.
description: Leon is playful, analytical, and more comfortable testing a system than trusting it on the first try. He documents train journeys in excessive detail, cooks excellent noodles, and claims video games taught him to accept failure gracefully.

questions.question: Which human bug would you never fix?
questions.answer: Laughing at the wrong moment. It causes trouble, but removing it would make people less interesting.

questions.question: What is the most spontaneous thing you have done?
questions.answer: Boarded the next train with one backpack and chose the destination after the doors closed.

clues.description: At 12:14 a.m. on all three disappearance nights, Leon's test phone generated 'Your room is ready' alerts for three demonstration hotels. The activity stayed inside a closed test system with invented guests and room numbers.
clues.developerExplanation: A nightly automated software test reproduces the exact time and phrase, but it never reaches the real hotel partner system.

clues.description: Leon's employer tests a hotel mobile-key application. His assigned project uses copies of hotel screens filled with fictional properties, guests, and reservations.
clues.developerExplanation: His profession explains close visual and wording matches while the isolated test environment blocks access to production bookings.

clues.description: A phone in Leon's profile photograph displays 'Your room is ready' above a 12:14 check-in. A visible DEMO banner and fake hotel name identify the screen as test data.
clues.developerExplanation: The photograph strongly resembles the victim messages, but the interface itself marks the record as a software demonstration.

clues.description: Leon jokes about a hotel-app test that runs every night at 12:14 and sends the default room-ready notification. Build records confirm that the check-ins used invented guests in an isolated test system.
clues.developerExplanation: His dating conversation naturally reveals the exact time and phrase; technical records then show that the resemblance never left the test environment.

lookingFor: A woman who is enthusiastic about something of her own, communicates directly, and does not treat dating like a checklist. I enjoy slow trust, spontaneous train trips, cooperative games, and anyone willing to admit that the first plan was not necessarily the best one.

name: Anton Keller
bio: I teach scales and collect songs that make ordinary days better.
description: Anton is a patient music teacher who can make scales sound less like punishment. He spends afternoons rehearsing student ensembles, collects odd little city sounds, and believes almost any bad day can be improved by coffee and a piano duet.
intent: Meet someone who loves good music

questions.question: Which song would you teach someone first?
questions.answer: Something with an easy left hand and a chorus worth getting wrong together. Confidence should arrive before technique.

questions.question: What makes a patient person impatient?
questions.answer: A metronome nobody admits is too loud. I can forgive missed notes much faster than fake concentration.

clues.description: Anton's school tablet played Glass Arcade, River Steps, and North Platform during afternoon rehearsals. Device permissions show playback access only, and each play occurred after the track had appeared publicly.
clues.developerExplanation: The three tracks look suspicious together, but the timestamps and playback-only school account exclude Anton from the private edits.

clues.description: A student recital Anton organized months earlier used Glass Arcade, River Steps, and North Platform as movements in a musical tour of the city.
clues.developerExplanation: The recital naturally explains Anton's familiarity with all three titles and predates the disappearances.

clues.description: A rehearsal photograph shows sheet music headed Glass Arcade / River Steps / North Platform beside a recital program dated four months before the first disappearance.
clues.developerExplanation: The image confirms that the location names belonged to Anton's earlier recital rather than a secret route learned from the victims.

clues.description: Anton describes the city recital and says the school tablet can play shared lists but cannot change them. School account records confirm both details.
clues.developerExplanation: His ordinary rehearsal story cross-checks with independent dates and access permissions.

redHerrings: Recital used the same three places
lookingFor: A woman who is warm, curious, and comfortable laughing through the awkward first minutes of meeting someone. She does not need to play an instrument, but I would love someone who brings me songs I would never find alone and has a favorite place to walk without a destination.

name: Milan Vogt
bio: I can recommend an album for every mood except indecision.
description: Milan runs a record shop that is tidy for roughly eleven minutes after opening. He likes handwritten recommendations, late closing shifts with one album playing front to back, and customers who return to argue politely about his choices.

questions.question: Which album would you save first?
questions.answer: The one my father pretended not to give me because he thought I should discover it myself. The sleeve is ruined; the record is perfect.

questions.question: What does your shop sound like after closing?
questions.answer: One full album, the receipt printer complaining, and me discovering three records that customers filed under pure imagination.

clues.description: The shop speakers streamed AFTER MIDNIGHT after midnight on all three disappearance nights. The store used a scheduled closing playlist from a follower account with no editing rights.
clues.developerExplanation: The timing is dramatic, but it reflects Milan's closing routine and a read-only commercial account.

clues.description: Milan's shop received an advance promotional pressing containing North Platform before it joined AFTER MIDNIGHT. Distributor records show the same copy went to forty-two shops.
clues.developerExplanation: Advance access to one track is legitimate and broadly shared; it does not explain the playlist edits or the other two endings.

clues.description: North Platform is visible behind Milan's counter in a photograph posted before the third disappearance. A promotional sticker and distributor number remain on its sleeve.
clues.developerExplanation: The photo makes the unreleased song look secret, but its marked promo sleeve supports Milan's innocent explanation.

clues.description: Milan says he schedules AFTER MIDNIGHT for late stocktaking and mentions the numbered North Platform promo. Store logs and the distributor list support him.
clues.developerExplanation: His chat reveals both suspicious details naturally, then records establish that neither gave him editor access.

lookingFor: A woman who has an opinionated record shelf, an easy sense of humor, and enough patience to browse without turning it into a race. I like direct people who can enjoy a quiet night, suggest the next song, and still tell me when my recommendation is completely wrong.

name: David Rehm
bio: I fix speakers, lose cables, and never skip the encore.
description: David works behind the sound desk at small venues and judges a night by how few people noticed him fixing it. He loves live music, old synthesizers, practical jokes that require no cleanup, and cooking while an entire album plays.
intent: See where a good conversation goes

questions.question: What sound should never be amplified?
questions.answer: Someone opening a snack during a quiet song. I have heard it through a stage microphone and still carry the memory.

questions.question: What makes a live show unforgettable?
questions.answer: One imperfect moment everyone shares. Perfect sound is satisfying; a room recovering together is what people remember.

clues.description: David's venue server stored Glass Arcade, River Steps, and North Platform as numbered soundcheck files. The showcase pack arrived six weeks before the first disappearance and contained no playlist credentials.
clues.developerExplanation: David possessed every instrumental, but a dated industry pack explains why and separates the files from the later private edits.

clues.description: David was sound technician for a label showcase where all three instrumentals were tested without titles. Venue paperwork lists them only as Soundcheck 4, 7, and 9.
clues.developerExplanation: His job placed the audio in his hands before the case, but not the later location names or listening data.

clues.description: A sound-desk photograph shows files 04_GLASS, 07_RIVER, and 09_NORTH in the playback history. The image metadata dates it six weeks before the first disappearance.
clues.developerExplanation: The picture confirms possession while its early timestamp makes the supposed case link innocent.

clues.description: David recalls a showcase pack with three unfinished instrumentals and says he learned their titles only later. The venue manifest confirms the numbered files and delivery date.
clues.developerExplanation: His story sounds specific because it comes from his work, but the manifest verifies the innocent timeline.

lookingFor: A woman who is independent, kind to tired service staff, and interested in the story behind how things work. A good date could be a concert, a late meal after it, or an evening comparing songs with production choices neither of us can unhear afterward.

name: Rafael Stein
bio: I draw people badly and buildings slightly better.
description: Rafael illustrates album covers and restaurant walls from a desk crowded with color cards. He is observant, slightly chaotic, and happiest when a client gives him one strange sentence and enough freedom to turn it into a picture.

questions.question: What color belongs to midnight?
questions.answer: Not black. Midnight is deep blue with one badly behaved orange light somewhere in the distance.

questions.question: What do you draw when nobody is paying?
questions.answer: Tiny maps of places I sat for too long. They are inaccurate but emotionally excellent.

clues.description: Rafael opened the AFTER MIDNIGHT admin preview twenty-three times. The invitation was comment-only and exposed cover art fields, not audio, listeners, history, or publishing controls.
clues.developerExplanation: Repeated admin-page access looks serious until the permission record shows Rafael could review artwork only.

clues.description: Rafael designed the AFTER MIDNIGHT cover from a brief built around three city landmarks: Glass Arcade, River Steps, and North Platform.
clues.developerExplanation: His direct link to the playlist and all three locations comes from a legitimate design commission.

clues.description: A desk photograph shows cover sketches connecting the three locations with a red line. The client brief beneath them is dated three months before the first disappearance.
clues.developerExplanation: The sketch resembles a planned route, but the dated art brief explains it and predates all victims.

clues.description: Rafael describes drawing the cover from a three-landmark brief and complains that his preview link could not play a single track. The invitation permissions agree.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural design complaint cross-checks with the restricted account record.

lookingFor: A woman who notices details, has a creative life of her own, and can disagree without making the evening heavy. I would gladly trade sketchbook pages for cafe recommendations, wander through an exhibition, and let her choose the color I have been avoiding.

name: Simon Brandt
bio: I know where the quiet shelves are and where the good coffee is.
description: Simon is a librarian who looks severe while shelving books and immediately ruins the effect with a terrible pun. He helps maintain a small city-sound archive, makes excellent coffee, and has never returned from a weekend trip without a local history book.

questions.question: Which book do you lend reluctantly?
questions.answer: My annotated city guide. People promise to ignore the notes, then return it with opinions about my handwriting.

questions.question: What sound belongs in a library?
questions.answer: Rain against tall windows. Page turning comes second; a distant printer losing an argument comes last.

clues.description: A library workstation searched waveform fingerprints for all three location tracks. Each search occurred the morning after that song appeared publicly on AFTER MIDNIGHT.
clues.developerExplanation: Simon investigated the audio, but only after publication; he could not have prepared or predicted the private changes.

clues.description: Simon helps catalogue field recordings made at Glass Arcade, River Steps, and North Platform for the municipal sound archive.
clues.developerExplanation: The archive explains why he recognized the tracks' background ambience without connecting him to the victims.

clues.description: An archive map pinned behind Simon marks the same three locations in the same order as the playlist. Its catalogue route was published two years earlier.
clues.developerExplanation: The matching route is visually suspicious but comes from an old public archive walk.

clues.description: Simon says he searched each new track because he recognized sounds from the archive walk. Search timestamps and the two-year-old map confirm that he reacted after release.
clues.developerExplanation: His curiosity creates a trail through all three songs, but the sequence is reactive rather than predictive.

lookingFor: A woman who enjoys thoughtful conversation, respects quiet without fearing it, and has at least one subject she could happily explain for an hour. I would choose a bookshop, a long coffee, and a walk through an overlooked part of the city over anything too polished.

name: Noel Hartl
bio: I repair bikes and take the long route whenever possible.
description: Noel repairs bicycles in a workshop where every radio is too dusty and every customer gets a free lecture about tire pressure. He prefers river paths to traffic, keeps old parts for improbable projects, and brings homemade sandwiches on long rides.

questions.question: Which route do you take when you are not in a hurry?
questions.answer: The river path past the old locks. It adds twenty minutes and removes most of the reasons I needed the ride.

questions.question: What makes something worth repairing?
questions.answer: A good story or good steel. Sentiment can save almost anything; bad metal rarely cooperates.

clues.description: Noel's workshop account uploaded a safety video containing the exact four-second phrase 'last stop home.' The upload predates AFTER MIDNIGHT by nine months and credits a public cycling campaign.
clues.developerExplanation: The rare audio sample appears on Noel's account, but the early public source shows he did not create it for the playlist.

clues.description: Noel volunteered for a night-cycling campaign whose slogan was 'Make the last stop home.' Its media pack included the spoken sample later used in the playlist.
clues.developerExplanation: His campaign work explains both the phrase and access to its recording long before the disappearances.

clues.description: A workshop photograph shows a campaign sticker reading LAST STOP: HOME on Noel's tool cabinet. The post is dated nine months before the playlist existed.
clues.developerExplanation: The phrase looks like a confession only when detached from the clearly dated safety campaign.

clues.description: Noel jokes about recording a safety-video voiceover after a long ride. The campaign archive contains his credited clip and confirms the much earlier date.
clues.developerExplanation: His dating story naturally exposes the sample while the archive proves it was public source material.

lookingFor: A woman who likes being outdoors, says what she wants, and understands that practical can still be romantic. I would enjoy a slow ride somewhere green, a picnic neither of us optimized, and hearing about the hobby she cares about more than anyone expects.

name: Julian Weiss
bio: I match songs to moments and remember exactly when people first heard them.
description: Julian curates playlists for venues and independent labels. He is calm, attentive, and unusually good at remembering the song someone mentioned once. He treats a playlist like a conversation: the opening earns attention, but the final track decides what remains.
intent: Looking for someone who pays attention

questions.question: What makes a memory stick?
questions.answer: A detail arriving at the exact moment you are ready for it. Usually a sound, sometimes a sentence, rarely the thing everyone planned.

questions.question: What is your rule for a perfect playlist?
questions.answer: Never waste the ending. The last track should feel so personal that the listener briefly believes it was waiting for them.

clues.description: Julian's personal device opened AFTER MIDNIGHT's private editor six to eight minutes before every final-track swap. Each session changed the ending and viewed the current listener before the corresponding disappearance.
clues.developerExplanation: Only Julian repeatedly combines editor access, live listener data, and the exact pre-disappearance timing.

clues.description: Julian describes himself as merely a follower of listener-made playlists. An archived profile screenshot from before the case displays an EDITOR badge beside AFTER MIDNIGHT.
clues.developerExplanation: The contradiction conceals his direct control of the playlist, though the profile alone does not prove how he used it.

clues.description: A studio photograph shows unreleased files named Glass Arcade, River Steps, and North Platform on Julian's monitor. The image was taken hours before the first of those endings became public.
clues.developerExplanation: Julian possessed the exact named endings before listeners or innocent followers could see them.

clues.description: Julian casually says he watches when a listener reaches the final song and can swap an ending live. He also names Glass Arcade, River Steps, and North Platform in their playlist order.
clues.developerExplanation: His ordinary explanation of curation exposes both the means and private sequence tied to all three disappearances.

lookingFor: A woman who is open-minded, quietly confident, and willing to share the songs she usually keeps private. I like late walks, small listening rooms, and people who notice how an evening changes when the right track arrives at exactly the right moment.

name: Felix Dorn
bio: I cut out the boring parts and sometimes forget real life has them.
description: Felix edits short films and can spend an hour choosing between two nearly identical seconds. Away from a screen, he enjoys night photography, loud breakfasts, neighborhood cinemas, and conversations that wander somewhere better than the original topic.

questions.question: What do you notice in a film before the story?
questions.answer: How people enter a room. A director tells you who has power before anyone says a word.

questions.question: Which part of the day would you cut?
questions.answer: The ten minutes spent looking for something already in my hand. Unfortunately, continuity insists they remain.

clues.description: Felix's editing project imported all three location instrumentals and night footage from the same places. A licensed media pack supplied every file two months before the first disappearance.
clues.developerExplanation: His project mirrors the playlist closely, but a dated commercial license explains the complete overlap.

clues.description: Felix cut a short film following a night journey from Glass Arcade to River Steps and North Platform for a tourism competition.
clues.developerExplanation: The film gives him knowledge of the route and music without granting playlist access or victim information.

clues.description: An editing-timeline photograph pairs all three instrumentals with footage of their matching locations. The project folder shows a creation date two months before the case.
clues.developerExplanation: The strongest-looking visual red herring is resolved by the older project timestamp and license receipt.

clues.description: Felix describes a night-city film built from a licensed route pack and remembers the three locations in order. The competition submission verifies the project date.
clues.developerExplanation: He knows the exact route for a public creative reason that existed before the disappearances.

redHerrings: Used all three tracks in a film
lookingFor: A woman who has a dry sense of humor, creative obsessions of her own, and no need to perform certainty. I would happily watch a strange film, walk home discussing the ending, and let her show me the ordinary place she thinks deserves a better camera angle.

name: Oskar Blum
bio: Good service is invisible, but a bad playlist never is.
description: Oskar manages a busy restaurant and still believes the staff meal matters more than the menu font. He likes jazz, early market trips, terrible travel stories, and the rare evening when somebody else chooses the music and books the table.

questions.question: What makes a restaurant feel alive?
questions.answer: A room where the staff can hear each other laugh. Perfect table settings do less than people think.

questions.question: Which table would you choose?
questions.answer: Near the kitchen but not in the traffic. You catch the energy and still get to finish a sentence.

clues.description: The restaurant group's account followed AFTER MIDNIGHT and played it at branches beside all three locations. Marketing controlled the account; Oskar's login could suggest tracks but could not publish or view listeners.
clues.developerExplanation: His work account spans the complete route, but permissions exclude him from the private edits and listener data.

clues.description: Oskar supervised evening shifts at restaurants near Glass Arcade, River Steps, and North Platform during the five-week period.
clues.developerExplanation: His branch rotation explains location overlap while scheduled shifts and staff records account for his presence.

clues.description: A staff-room screen in Oskar's photograph displays AFTER MIDNIGHT beneath a three-branch route map. The publishing controls are assigned to an external marketing agency.
clues.developerExplanation: The image combines the playlist and route but also supports the limited business-use explanation.

clues.description: Oskar explains choosing music suggestions for three branches while an agency controls the actual account. Permission logs and staff rosters confirm the split.
clues.developerExplanation: His conversation clarifies why he knows the list yet cannot alter it.

lookingFor: A woman who is direct, considerate, and able to enjoy food without turning dinner into a review. I appreciate people who have their own plans, laugh at small disasters, and would rather discover a neighborhood restaurant than queue for the place everyone photographed.

name: Lukas Falk
bio: I study by day and make overly ambitious dinner plans at night.
description: Lukas studies urban planning and organizes a campus music club with more enthusiasm than administrative skill. He likes cheap noodles, public transport maps, small gigs, and learning a city's personality by missing the correct tram once.

questions.question: What are you learning outside university?
questions.answer: How to cook for six people without making six portions of the same mistake. The music club is patient with me.

questions.question: What meal proves someone made an effort?
questions.answer: Anything chopped by hand after a long day. It can be ugly; effort has a recognizable shape.

clues.description: Lukas re-shared AFTER MIDNIGHT to a campus music group that included two later victims. The public share exposed neither private listening sessions nor editor controls.
clues.developerExplanation: The social connection is real, but Lukas distributed a public link and could not monitor individual listeners.

clues.description: Campus records show Lukas knew two victims casually through the music club and attended a student event at North Platform with one of them.
clues.developerExplanation: He overlaps socially with two listeners, not all three, and the documented group setting explains the contact.

clues.description: A campus-event photograph places Lukas and one victim beneath the North Platform sign. Forty-three club members appear in the original event album.
clues.developerExplanation: The image seems personal when cropped, but the full album establishes a large public club event.

clues.description: Lukas says he shared the playlist with his music club and knew two members who liked it. Club membership and link records confirm a broad public share, not private tracking.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural club story explains both the victims and playlist without supplying the killer's access.

redHerrings: Knew two listeners through the club
lookingFor: A woman who is curious, playful, and comfortable building a life while both people are still figuring things out. I would choose a small concert, an unplanned meal, and a long conversation about the place she wants to see next over anything formal.

name: Emil Kranz
bio: I keep departures moving and always arrive early in my own life.
description: Emil keeps trains moving from a control room full of clocks that never quite agree. He is precise at work, relaxed everywhere else, and happiest with strong coffee, an old railway map, and enough time to hear how somebody's day really went.

questions.question: What makes waiting easier?
questions.answer: Knowing whether it will be three minutes or thirty. After that, coffee and the right company solve most of it.

questions.question: Which rule do you secretly appreciate?
questions.answer: Arrive two minutes early. Not enough to look anxious, just enough to notice the room before it notices you.

clues.description: The Platform 0 display override executed through Emil's dispatch console at 00:06. Badge and console records show he left the room at 23:54 for a signal fault; the override was queued three minutes later by an unnamed simulation job.
clues.developerExplanation: Emil's console displayed the false destination, but the job was inserted after he left and could have been pushed through the transit simulation bridge.

clues.description: Emil can approve emergency display messages but cannot create destinations, issue digital tickets, or grant access through staff gates.
clues.developerExplanation: His role explains the display connection while separating him from the ticket and physical access needed for Mara's trap.

clues.description: A control-room photograph contains P0 on a diagnostic board. The uncropped monthly test sheet cycles every placeholder code from P0 through P9 and predates Mara's attack by five months.
clues.developerExplanation: The photograph looks like prior knowledge of Platform 0, but P0 was a routine placeholder on a documented test board.

clues.description: Emil describes leaving his console to inspect a signal fault during the overnight display test. The incident sheet and another dispatcher's badge log confirm his location when the override was queued.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural work story cross-checks with independent records and explains why his signed-in console remained involved.

name: Hannes Wolf
bio: I draw cities that people can actually enjoy walking through.
description: Hannes plans streets and public spaces, then spends weekends testing whether they are pleasant to walk through. He likes museums with good benches, hand-drawn maps, and conversations that change his mind without becoming a competition.

questions.question: Which public place feels welcoming?
questions.answer: A square with shade, somewhere to sit, and more than one reason to remain after you finish your coffee.

questions.question: What do maps fail to show?
questions.answer: Whether a street feels kind at night. Width and lighting help, but people remember atmosphere more than measurements.

clues.developerExplanation: The title is suspicious, but the publicly available planning file lacks the hidden route and current access details.

name: Bastian Reiter
bio: I know every shortcut and still occasionally miss my own front door.
description: Bastian delivers urgent parcels by bicycle and knows which shortcuts are useful versus merely exciting. He is quick with a joke, loyal to his favorite food trucks, and surprisingly content to spend a free evening going nowhere at all.
intent: Meet someone who likes the city

questions.question: What belongs in the perfect delivery bag?
questions.answer: A rain jacket, two emergency snacks, and one pen that has not mysteriously joined another courier.

questions.question: How do you recover from a wrong turn?
questions.answer: Stop pretending it was intentional, check the map, and find one good thing you would have missed on the correct route.

description: Gregor designs stations and civic buildings with a quiet conviction that entrances matter more than facades. He enjoys classical music, old gardens, and books containing somebody else's notes in the margins.

questions.question: Which unfinished thing do you still love?
questions.answer: A small station pavilion that lost its funding halfway through. The roof exists only on paper, but it is still one of my best rooms.

questions.question: What makes an entrance inviting?
questions.answer: You understand where to go without being ordered. Good buildings offer direction and let people keep their dignity.

description: Timo is an apprentice electrician who can repair a lighting circuit and still forget to charge his own phone. He plays football badly but enthusiastically, experiments with one-pan dinners, and considers a sunny park bench a perfectly respectable plan.

questions.question: What do you always forget to charge?
questions.answer: My phone, despite working with electricity all day. Expertise apparently refuses to follow me home.

questions.question: Which small skill feels surprisingly useful?
questions.answer: Knowing which switch not to touch. It sounds unimpressive until the room is dark and everyone has an opinion.

name: Henrik Moser
bio: I check tickets and collect stories from people who missed trains.
description: Henrik checks tickets for a living and collects the stories people offer when they have the wrong one. He is observant without being severe, prefers tea to station coffee, and keeps a small cabinet of retired railway stamps and signs.

questions.question: What is the best excuse for missing a train?
questions.answer: The honest one. Although 'I was helping a stranger carry a cello' remains difficult to argue with.

questions.question: What object can hold an entire story?
questions.answer: An old ticket. A time, a destination, and sometimes a coffee stain are enough for the imagination to do the rest.

name: Stefan Krüger

questions.question: What pattern do people usually miss?
questions.answer: The small decision before the obvious one. By the time a journey looks unusual, its direction was often decided much earlier.

questions.question: What makes a city feel private?
questions.answer: The few minutes after the last crowd leaves. Familiar streets become quieter versions of themselves, almost as if they were waiting.

questions.question: How do you rescue a bad morning?
questions.answer: Open a window, make something hot, and complete one small task before the day gets another vote.

questions.question: What smell feels like home?
questions.answer: Bread five minutes before it is ready. Coffee is my work; bread still feels like someone is waiting for you.

questions.answer: Nettles. Useful, resilient, and judged almost entirely by one bad first impression.

questions.question: What mistake do beginners make with plants?

questions.question: Which weather improves a city?

questions.question: Which shortcut earns your trust?
questions.answer: One that still works in rain and does not depend on a gatekeeper being in a generous mood.

questions.answer: Glass. It remembers every rushed decision and presents the mistake beautifully in the finished object.

questions.question: Which room needs better light?
questions.answer: Almost every restaurant after sunset. Atmosphere should not require guessing what arrived on the plate.

questions.answer: Conditions matter more than promises. Give something the environment it needs and behavior becomes remarkably predictable.

questions.answer: Heavy rain. It makes the room feel sealed away while everything outside becomes less certain.

clues.description: Christoph explains that three black bruises across a white orchid mean it was crushed inside a closed left hand. Lena was found holding three blackened petals in her left palm, a detail withheld from every public report.
clues.developerExplanation: His seemingly professional observation reproduces the private physical detail from Lena's final moments.

redHerrings: Inserted old footage into the live feed
Knew Lena had crushed the flower
lookingFor: A woman who is self-possessed, observant, and comfortable letting trust develop slowly. I appreciate quiet confidence, thoughtful disagreement, and evenings where the setting feels private even when the city is close.

name: Patrick Wolf
bio: I wait for the right light and take too many pictures of paths.
description: Patrick photographs landscapes by waiting longer than most people consider reasonable. He notices paths, reflections, and changing light, then balances the quiet work with films, crowded cafes, and conversations that move faster than he does behind a camera.

questions.question: How long would you wait for one photograph?
questions.answer: Until the light changes or my coffee becomes genuinely unpleasant. Patience still needs a practical limit.

questions.question: Which place changes most in rain?
questions.answer: A glass building. The view disappears, reflections take over, and suddenly the inside becomes the landscape.

clues.description: Patrick's camera archive contains the exact fourteen-minute recording inserted into the 2:13 feed. He delivered the finished Rain Room files to Central Glasshouse three weeks earlier, and his client folder became read-only after transfer.
clues.developerExplanation: Patrick created the material used for the false alibi, placing him in the intended shortlist. File permissions show he could not later insert it into the live channel.

clues.description: Patrick was the official photographer for the Rain Room promotion and directed Christoph through several repeated plant-care actions for the camera.
clues.developerExplanation: He staged the authentic source scene but had no reason to know it would later be presented as live security footage.

clues.description: Patrick's contact sheet contains the same coat movement, tool placement, and artificial rain pattern seen in the alibi clip. The sequence is dated three weeks before Lena's death.
clues.developerExplanation: The image proves he filmed the old scene while also fixing his involvement to the harmless promotional date.

clues.description: Patrick describes waiting through an artificial-rain shoot while a manager repeated the same watering movement for fourteen minutes. Contract delivery and read-only archive records confirm his limited role.
clues.developerExplanation: His chat reveals why his footage matches perfectly and why he no longer controlled the delivered copy.

redHerrings: Recorded the footage used as alibi
lookingFor: A woman who is curious, comfortable with silence, and willing to stop when something ordinary becomes beautiful. I would enjoy a walk with no photographic objective, a film afterward, and coffee somewhere neither of us needs to document.

name: Stefan Bär
bio: I sell plants and give advice nobody asked for.
description: Stefan runs a garden centre and gives plant advice with the confidence of someone who has watched customers ignore it for years. He enjoys market mornings, family recipes, bird calls, and conversations that remain friendly even when opinions do not.

questions.question: What advice do people ignore most often?
questions.answer: Buy the plant that suits your window, not the one that looked best beneath professional lighting.

questions.question: Which plant is hardest to sell?
questions.answer: The honest one. A slow-growing plant with one excellent leaf loses every popularity contest beside instant flowers.

clues.description: Stefan's point-of-sale account approved the rare white orchid later delivered to Lena. The prepaid order hid the recipient from his screen and arrived through Central Glasshouse's shared trade-purchasing alias.
clues.developerExplanation: Stefan supplied the exact flower, but the purchasing trail originates from a shared glasshouse account and gives him no knowledge of Lena.

clues.description: Stefan's garden centre is the region's main commercial supplier of the white orchid cultivar, selling cut stems to research gardens and florists.
clues.developerExplanation: His stock explains the pollen source while broad institutional sales prevent exclusive possession.

clues.description: A market photograph shows a tray of the same white orchids behind Stefan. Inventory records assign the stem used in Lena's order to a florist pickup later that day.
clues.developerExplanation: The photograph establishes supply, and the numbered inventory continues the chain into the florist's custody.

clues.description: Stefan mentions approving an unusually expensive anonymous trade order without seeing its final recipient. The purchase record and pickup camera confirm the order passed directly to the florist.
clues.developerExplanation: His sales anecdote reveals the anonymous order but not control over its arrangement, delivery, or message.

redHerrings: Accepted an order without recipient name
Buyer used a glasshouse trade account
lookingFor: A woman who is warm, practical, and willing to say when advice is unwanted. I would happily cook a family recipe, browse a weekend market, and spend an afternoon outside without trying to turn it into an achievement.

name: Leo Maurer
bio: I arrange flowers and rearrange my plans at the last minute.
description: Leo is learning floristry one imperfect arrangement at a time. He is adaptable, musical, and better at choosing flowers for other people's feelings than explaining his own without several attempts.

questions.question: Which flower is misunderstood?
questions.answer: Carnations. They last, they travel well, and people blame them for being affordable as though loyalty should be expensive.

questions.question: What makes a gift feel personal?
questions.answer: One detail that could only belong to the receiver. Price is much less convincing than attention.

clues.description: Leo's shop terminal printed Lena's address label and a blank message card for the anonymous orchid. The prepaid web order imported automatically, exposing no purchaser name or dating-profile information to the shop.
clues.developerExplanation: Leo assembled the flower sent to Lena, but the ordering system deliberately concealed the buyer from him.

clues.description: As the apprentice on duty, Leo wrapped the single orchid stem in moss and glassine according to instructions attached to the online order.
clues.developerExplanation: His direct handling explains packaging traces while the standardized order controls every meaningful choice.

clues.description: A workbench photograph shows Leo beside the finished white-orchid box and blank card. Shop video continues through sealing and courier handoff without the package reopening.
clues.developerExplanation: The image appears incriminating when isolated, but continuous footage preserves the package chain after his routine preparation.

clues.description: Leo describes disliking blank cards and following a strangely precise anonymous order because apprentices cannot rewrite paid instructions. The shop video and automatic import log support him.
clues.developerExplanation: His conversation naturally reveals the cardless arrangement while confirming he never learned who ordered it.

lookingFor: A woman who is expressive, kind about small mistakes, and interested in building something more real than an impressive first message. I would enjoy baking together, sharing music, and giving each other plans we are allowed to rearrange.

name: Tobias Kern
bio: I plan elegant weekends for other people and lose my own train tickets with impressive consistency.
description: Tobias turns complicated journeys into simple plans, then treats his own free time with much less discipline. He is quick-witted, considerate, and happiest when a map leaves room for an unplanned meal.

questions.question: What makes a trip worth planning?
questions.answer: Enough structure to prevent disaster and enough empty space for the place to surprise you.

questions.question: What always gets left off an itinerary?
questions.answer: The hour you need after something wonderful, when rushing to the next stop would ruin it.

clues.description: At 18:42, Tobias exported the event timetable from his travel-planning account. Its hidden revision history contains a field named WILDCARD BUFFER, but that field was created in Martin's original template and renamed GROUP PHOTO BREAK by Tobias.
clues.developerExplanation: The ominous wording is inherited metadata. Version authorship and the final ten-round schedule clear Tobias.

clues.description: Tobias attended Ten Chances and volunteered to turn the organizer checklist into a readable timetable. He could see the planned rounds but never handled completed scorecards or sound controls.
clues.developerExplanation: His planning role explains access to the schedule without providing the means to select or summon Elisa.

clues.description: The final group photograph places Tobias beside the scorecard collection box. A wider image shows him returning a marker while staff carry the sealed cards away.
clues.developerExplanation: A cropped image looks suspicious, but the sequence shows no access to the submitted cards.

clues.description: Tobias recalls deleting a dramatic wildcard label from a client template because it only meant spare time for photographs. File history confirms Martin authored the original field.
clues.developerExplanation: The conversation naturally explains the inherited planning term and points authorship back to Martin.

lookingFor: A woman who enjoys making plans without treating them as laws. I value curiosity, good humor when something goes wrong, and someone who would rather discover one memorable street than collect ten landmarks.

name: Erik Scholz
bio: I remember faces, breakfast orders, and the exact moment someone realizes checkout was an hour ago.
description: Erik works a hotel front desk and occasionally helps with guest reception at private events. He is sociable without being loud, cooks when his shifts allow it, and remembers small preferences long after introductions.
intent: Looking for something warm and direct

questions.question: What makes a welcome feel genuine?
questions.answer: Remembering one small thing from the last conversation instead of performing a perfect greeting.

questions.question: Which detail about people stays with you?
questions.answer: Usually what they ordered while nervous. Nobody chooses tea with that much concentration when relaxed.

clues.description: At 21:14, Erik's reception terminal opened Guest 27's phone-pouch record. Lobby video shows him at the desk throughout, checking the record only after Elisa failed to join the phone-return queue.
clues.developerExplanation: The access happened in response to Elisa being missing, not before she entered the booth.

clues.developerExplanation: He knew Elisa was Guest 27 but lacked access to the mechanism used to summon her.

clues.description: A photograph shows Erik wearing the phone-cabinet key beside the event entrance. The key inventory identifies a separate shape and serial series from the booth service key.
clues.developerExplanation: The visible key is real but opens the wrong secured area.

clues.description: Erik mentions that one unclaimed numbered pouch kept him late after a singles event. Desk video and the cabinet audit confirm he immediately notified the venue manager.
clues.developerExplanation: He reveals the record access naturally, and independent logs show a responsible response.

redHerrings: Desk camera keeps him in the lobby
lookingFor: A woman who communicates clearly, laughs easily, and notices the difference between politeness and real attention. I would enjoy quiet dinners, old films, and the occasional run that becomes a long walk.

name: Moritz Lang
bio: I cook for crowds on weekends and spend Monday pretending I am happy with leftovers.
description: Moritz runs pop-up kitchens for markets and private gatherings. He is generous, irreverent, and incapable of discussing food without suggesting that everybody share at least one plate.
intent: Looking for an appetite for life

questions.question: What dish is worth waiting for?
questions.answer: Anything braised slowly enough that the whole building knows dinner is coming.

questions.question: What belongs in every shared kitchen?
questions.answer: One reliable knife, too many wooden spoons, and permission to admit a recipe needs help.

clues.description: Moritz's temporary staff badge opened the storage room adjoining the photo booth at 21:09. Kitchen video shows him return sixty-eight seconds later carrying two ice buckets requested before the final round.
clues.developerExplanation: His proximity is suspicious, but continuous kitchen footage makes the short supply trip complete and verifiable.

clues.description: Moritz catered Ten Chances and used the booth-side storage room for ice and serving trays. The room shares a wall with the booth but has no opening into its rear service panel.

clues.description: A staff photograph shows Moritz carrying a long black case behind the event curtain. The next frame shows it open and filled with carving tools returned to the supervised kitchen station.

clues.description: Moritz complains about a last-minute ice run during a singles dinner and remembers the kitchen timer continuing without him. Video timestamps and the order ticket support the one-minute trip.
clues.developerExplanation: A natural catering anecdote resolves both the room access and his exact timing.

redHerrings: Camera shows a one-minute ice run
lookingFor: A woman who is expressive, kind to service workers, and comfortable sharing both food and opinions. Complicated schedules are manageable; pretending not to care is much harder for me.

name: Kilian Vogt
bio: I know the safe trail, the scenic trail, and the trail I recommend only after learning how honest you are about hills.
description: Kilian leads climbing and hiking groups, where calm decisions matter more than impressive stories. Away from work he is playful, competitive over tea, and unusually serious about keeping promises.

questions.question: What makes a trail memorable?
questions.answer: The conversation beside you. A spectacular view becomes surprisingly ordinary when nobody can share the silence.

questions.question: Which risk is worth taking?
questions.answer: Saying what you want before certainty arrives. Most other risks improve when carefully reduced first.

clues.description: Kilian and Elisa had matched online before Ten Chances. At 18:21, his phone saved an unsent draft reading, 'You did not even give me a chance,' after she said they should keep the event comfortable.
clues.developerExplanation: The frustrated draft creates motive but never left his device, which was sealed before the event began.

clues.description: Kilian was the sixth scheduled date for Elisa. Her carbon copy marks NO beside his name, and two neighboring tables remember an awkward but quiet ending to their round.
clues.developerExplanation: Rejection makes him emotionally plausible, but his movements remain public and documented.

clues.description: In the final group photograph, Kilian appears to be gripping the numbered card belonging to Elisa. A second angle identifies the object as his own folded event badge with a similar coral border.
clues.developerExplanation: The visual resemblance is intentional misdirection resolved by another angle.

clues.description: Kilian admits handling an uncomfortable encounter with a previous online connection at a group event by giving her space. Table witnesses and the sealed-phone log support his account.
clues.developerExplanation: He sounds human rather than perfectly composed, while independent details clear the threatening interpretation.

redHerrings: Received a NO on her scorecard
Witnesses keep him in the hall
lookingFor: A woman who can be direct without being cruel and adventurous without making recklessness a personality. I like shared effort, honest refusals, and tea strong enough to survive a cold morning.

name: Rene Adler
bio: I build tables, repair old cabinets, and still own one chair that should have been thrown away years ago.
description: Rene restores furniture with the patience of someone who expects every object to conceal at least one bad repair. He is gentle, dryly funny, and more interested in how things are made than what they cost.

questions.question: What should be repaired instead of replaced?
questions.answer: Anything whose damage belongs to its story rather than making it unsafe to use.

questions.question: What makes a table inviting?
questions.answer: Enough space for elbows, warm light, and no decoration too precious to move for another plate.

clues.description: At 17:48, Rene's service account marked the vintage booth OUT OF ORDER after its rear latch failed inspection. The master key assigned to him opened that panel at 21:08, one minute after Elisa entered.

clues.developerExplanation: His specialist access makes him a serious candidate until custody of the key is established.

clues.description: A workshop photograph shows Rene standing inside the booth with its rear panel open. The dated repair sequence also shows Martin collecting the closed cabinet after the final inspection.
clues.developerExplanation: The image proves knowledge of the route but also documents transfer of the booth.

clues.description: Rene recalls refusing to approve an old photo booth after its rear latch slipped, then making the renter sign for its only service key. The repair invoice and signature from Martin confirm the handoff.
clues.developerExplanation: His conversation supplies the missing chain of custody and converts a strong access clue into a resolved red herring.

redHerrings: Built the booth's rear access panel
Marked the booth out of service
Transferred the service key to Martin
lookingFor: A woman who values patience, asks thoughtful questions, and has interests she could happily explain for an hour. I prefer affection that becomes visible through consistency rather than spectacle.

name: Valentin Roth
bio: I tell official stories for work and collect the better unofficial ones over coffee afterward.
description: Valentin guides historical tours and hosts occasional cultural events. He is articulate, theatrical in small doses, and happiest when a prepared plan creates room for an unscripted conversation.

questions.question: When does a story improve in the retelling?
questions.answer: When the teller understands it better, not when the inconvenient parts quietly disappear.

questions.question: When should a guide stop talking?
questions.answer: Just before the view, the music, or the person beside them can say something better.

clues.description: Valentin's host console contains the exact voice line used to summon Guest 27 and an audio file with eleven bells. Its input log records no trigger after the tenth round; both files were exported to Martin's photo tablet during soundcheck.
clues.developerExplanation: His voice and console look decisive until the transfer log shows another device possessed and played the material.

clues.description: Valentin hosted Ten Chances, announced each rotation, and controlled the ten scheduled bells. He also recorded several promotional phrases requested by the event photographer.
clues.developerExplanation: The role grants voice and normal sound access, making him an intentionally strong but fair false lead.

clues.description: The final group image captures Valentin beside the sound console when the wildcard announcement begins. A continuous event video shows both hands occupied while the console screen remains on its completed schedule.
clues.developerExplanation: The still image suggests control; the longer recording shows no manual action.

clues.description: Valentin jokes about recording dozens of generic prompts for a singles-night soundcheck, including a wildcard invitation he considered too dramatic. The production request and export record name the tablet belonging to Martin.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural hosting anecdote explains how his voice was copied and who received the recording.

lookingFor: A woman who enjoys stories but does not mistake confidence for certainty. I appreciate quick humor, long walks, and people who are comfortable changing the subject when something real appears.

name: Martin Seifert
bio: I photograph places before crowds arrive and celebrations after everyone forgets the camera is there.
description: Martin moves easily between travel assignments and private events. He is attentive, reassuring, and skilled at making nervous people feel that nothing awkward has been noticed.

questions.question: What makes a photograph honest?
questions.answer: The instant after someone thinks the picture has already been taken and stops arranging their face.

questions.question: What would you never crop from a picture?
questions.answer: The person watching from the edge. Attention often explains more than whatever was placed in the center.

clues.developerExplanation: The device sequence gives Martin knowledge of the choices made by Elisa and direct control over both impossible event actions.

clues.developerExplanation: He speaks as a possible date rather than an accused man, but his ordinary work history completes the serial connection.

lookingFor: A woman who is self-possessed, observant, and willing to let trust develop without performing enthusiasm. I admire people who make deliberate choices and stand by them.

name: Jan Bruck
bio: I know where every train should be and have developed emotional resilience about where it actually is.
description: Jan works regional rail and treats delays with practical humor rather than optimism. He likes chess, experimental baking, and journeys where nobody needs to sprint during the final thirty seconds.

questions.question: What makes a journey feel shorter?
questions.answer: A conversation that survives the quiet parts without anyone reaching automatically for a screen.

questions.question: What do timetables never explain?
questions.answer: Which missed connection becomes a disaster and which one becomes the best hour of the trip.

clues.description: At 21:05, Jan's event badge appears at Table 3 although his assigned place for the group photograph was Table 8. An incident note records that he exchanged badges after red wine soaked his original card.
clues.developerExplanation: The location discrepancy comes from a documented badge replacement, not physical movement.

clues.developerExplanation: His natural admission resolves the location anomaly without making him implausibly perfect.

His coat was seen beside the booth
Group photo keeps him in the hall
lookingFor: A woman who can make decisions without turning every choice into a test. Reliability attracts me, but so does somebody willing to laugh when a careful plan meets reality.

name: Benedikt Haas
bio: I deliver dinner across the city and still manage to discover at midnight that I forgot my own.
description: Benedikt cycles courier shifts while saving for a small recording setup. He is energetic, curious, and capable of turning an ordinary route into a competition nobody else agreed to enter.

questions.question: What deserves a bicycle detour?
questions.answer: A bakery with one excellent thing and no interest in becoming a fashionable destination.

questions.question: Which game reveals too much?
questions.answer: Any cooperative game. Losing together shows character much faster than winning alone.

clues.description: Benedikt's courier scan delivered a parcel containing blank wildcard cards and the booth's square embossing stamp at 18:02. The sealed handoff was signed on Martin's photo tablet.
clues.developerExplanation: He transported critical materials but had neither knowledge of their use nor access after delivery.

clues.description: Benedikt remembers a photographer insisting on personally signing for a surprisingly heavy stationery parcel. Route video and the digital receipt identify Martin as that recipient.
clues.developerExplanation: The harmless courier story establishes a clean handoff to the person who later used the materials.

redHerrings: Martin signed for the sealed package
lookingFor: A woman who is curious, emotionally direct, and willing to be enthusiastic without pretending everything is effortless. Shared music helps, but mutual kindness matters more than matching playlists.

name: Rolf Mader
bio: I retired with plans to slow down and immediately filled the calendar with books, gardens, and ambitious dinners.
description: Rolf taught literature for three decades and now enjoys having opinions without grading anyone else. He is reflective, warm, and willing to begin again even when being a beginner feels undignified.
intent: Looking for a patient new chapter

questions.question: What did teaching change about you?
questions.answer: It taught me that silence can mean confusion, resistance, thought, or courage, and guessing which one is usually arrogant.

questions.question: Which book deserves another reading?
questions.answer: The one you loved too young. Sometimes the book changes because the reader finally catches up.

clues.developerExplanation: The historic overlap is unsettling but ends well before the critical window of the earlier event.

clues.description: The preserved scorecard belonging to Rolf marks YES beside the missing woman, while her carbon copy marks NO beside him. No later message or connection exists between their accounts.

Transit record shows he left early
lookingFor: A woman who has built a life she respects and still has room for something unexpected. I value patience, intellectual playfulness, and meals long enough for the conversation to change direction.

name: Armin Keller
bio: I improve delivery routes for a living and still take the longest possible way to my favorite coffee shop.
description: Armin measures streets, stairways, and walking times for regional delivery networks. He is practical, gently competitive, and happiest when a precise map leads somewhere pleasantly unplanned.

questions.question: Which route is worth taking twice?
questions.answer: The one that changes with the weather. Familiar should not have to mean predictable.

questions.question: What makes a map feel personal?
questions.answer: The notes in the margins: reliable coffee, a quiet bench, and the corner where someone once waited for you.

clues.description: A profile photograph places Armin beside a survey marker on the street where Nora lived. The uncropped image and work order identify the opposite block and a timestamp forty-eight hours earlier.

clues.description: Armin recalls a tedious team survey ending at a coffee shop in the same delivery district. The city assignment and four synchronized GPS tracks confirm the ordinary reason for his route.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural work story independently supports the scheduled survey and continuous team presence.

Team route log confirms the survey
lookingFor: A woman who enjoys curiosity without turning everything into a competition. I value calm confidence, honest plans, and someone who can appreciate a long route without needing every minute explained.

name: Marius Vogt
bio: I notice exits before menus and am trying to become less professionally annoying about restaurant lighting.
description: Marius evaluates access systems for apartments and small businesses. Away from work he is relaxed, attentive, and more interested in cooking for friends than explaining what their locks are doing wrong.

questions.question: What makes somewhere feel safe?
questions.answer: Knowing you can leave, knowing you are welcome to stay, and not having either fact repeatedly announced.

questions.question: Which rule do you break at home?
questions.answer: I leave the kitchen window open while cooking, despite having delivered several lectures about exactly that habit.

lookingFor: A woman who is direct, emotionally steady, and comfortable disagreeing without making affection conditional. I like quiet films, loud kitchens, and plans that remain enjoyable when they change.

name: Lennart Wolf
bio: I draw maps, cycle everywhere, and occasionally become lost with enough confidence to look intentional.
description: Lennart studies cartography and illustrates small neighborhood guides for local shops. He is curious, self-deprecating, and prone to giving handmade details more attention than expensive gestures.

questions.question: What belongs on a map but rarely appears?
questions.answer: Where the pavement becomes quiet enough to hear yourself think.

questions.question: What is your favorite handmade gift?
questions.answer: A badly drawn map to a picnic. The proportions were hopeless, but every landmark was a shared joke.
