Map ends far from her building
lookingFor: A woman who asks unexpected questions, enjoys making things, and does not confuse polish with sincerity. Books, bicycles, and long museum afternoons would all be welcome company.

name: Nils Hartmann
bio: I ask uncomfortable questions at work and try to leave them out of dinner unless somebody is genuinely interested.
description: Nils writes about municipal decisions, forgotten neighborhoods, and people who disappear between official systems. He is empathetic, persistent, and much funnier away from a deadline than his serious work suggests.

questions.question: Which story deserves more attention?
questions.answer: The quiet one that changed the life of somebody without becoming dramatic enough for a headline.

questions.question: When should a question remain unanswered?
questions.answer: When answering would satisfy curiosity but cost another person something they never agreed to give.

clues.description: Nils searched the municipal archive for both Amelie Rauch and Klara Weiss during the month before Nora's death. His editor calendar and source log place the searches inside a documented article about unresolved local records.
clues.developerExplanation: He knew both names, but his interest developed through accountable reporting and began independently of Nora.

clues.description: Nils kept scanned copies of correspondence from both older files after his article was postponed. Every page carries an archive watermark and checkout record.
clues.developerExplanation: Possessing both histories is suspicious, but provenance is complete and no page includes the address of Nora.

clues.description: A photograph on the desk belonging to Nils includes folders labeled RAUCH and WEISS. Image metadata matches a supervised archive visit recorded by the municipal clerk.
clues.developerExplanation: The picture proves research rather than secret personal contact.

clues.description: Nils talks about an unfinished article comparing two old files that different departments never examined together. Editor notes and interview recordings account for every source he used.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural professional frustration explains why he found the historical names before their connection became public.

redHerrings: Source logs predate the letter programme
lookingFor: A woman who has strong interests of her own, values kindness over charm, and can move between serious conversation and ridiculous humor without treating either as an act.

name: Konrad Stein
bio: I move complicated paperwork across borders and keep my weekends as local as possible.
description: Konrad resolves shipping problems for galleries, small manufacturers, and private forwarding services. He is precise, understated, and considerably more playful once nobody is waiting for a customs form.

questions.question: Which detail is always worth checking twice?
questions.answer: The one everybody calls obvious. Confidence is where small administrative disasters like to hide.

questions.question: What makes an evening feel uncomplicated?
questions.answer: Tea, one person, and no conversation that begins with a tracking number.

clues.description: At 16:31, Konrad's broker account opened the anonymous forwarding batch containing Nora's tenth reply and decoded its district sorting zone. A supervisor-approved customs audit required the lookup, but the visible route stopped before the final street.
clues.developerExplanation: He accessed the correct batch and understands its codes, making him dangerous until the technical limit of that access is verified.

clues.description: Konrad advises the forwarding centre on parcels that cross customs boundaries. His tools can reveal regional hubs and delivery districts but deliberately receive no last-mile recipient table.
clues.developerExplanation: His role explains batch access without granting the exact address of Nora.

clues.description: A desk photograph exposes part of the address-translation key used by Letters First. The visible columns resolve depot and district codes; the street-address column exists only on the postal carrier system.
clues.developerExplanation: The image looks like a privacy breach but demonstrates the same technical boundary as his account.

clues.description: Konrad complains about auditing an anonymous correspondence batch whose labels became useless after the district code. The work ticket and mirrored terminal log confirm he never opened a last-mile address.
clues.developerExplanation: His conversation supplies an independently recorded limit rather than relying on his denial.

redHerrings: Audit never exposed her street address
lookingFor: A woman who respects boundaries, communicates clearly, and finds satisfaction in quiet competence. I like gardens, patient games, and plans with no hidden test inside them.

name: Fabian Roth
bio: I map landscapes from above and still spend several minutes each morning looking for my keys.
description: Fabian builds and repairs compact survey drones for parks and construction sites. He is inventive, energetic, and happiest when technical work gives way to games, open air, or unapologetically childish snacks.

questions.question: Which piece of technology feels like magic?
questions.answer: Anything that quietly prevents a mistake instead of demanding applause for doing something unnecessary.

questions.question: What do you enjoy doing badly?
questions.answer: Drawing. My drones make precise maps, so my terrible sketches feel like a small personal rebellion.

clues.description: Fabian's supplier account purchased twelve miniature Bluetooth trackers matching the circular recess in Nora's wax fragment. His inventory initially lists only eleven, while a twelfth radio identifier continues transmitting from a damaged survey drone.
clues.developerExplanation: The hardware match and missing inventory are strong until the unique radio record locates the device elsewhere.

clues.description: Fabian can conceal miniature trackers inside drone housings and translate their signals into precise coordinates. His workshop inventory uses numbered radio identifiers for every unit.
clues.developerExplanation: He can perform the tracking portion of the method, but not the paper work or historical correspondence.

clues.description: A profile photograph shows a loose tracker identical in size to the wax cavity. Enlarged serial digits match the unit later recorded inside survey drone D-14, not the missing envelope device.
clues.developerExplanation: The physical resemblance is real while the identifier points to innocent equipment.

clues.description: Fabian remembers losing a tracker during a rushed drone repair and finding its signal inside the battery housing days later. Repair video and continuous telemetry verify the embarrassing mistake.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural workshop anecdote resolves the apparent inventory gap with device-specific proof.

redHerrings: Bought trackers matching the wax cavity
Radio ID remained in a survey drone
lookingFor: A woman who is warm, independent, and willing to admit when enthusiasm has outrun expertise. Shared curiosity matters more to me than matching hobbies perfectly.

name: Viktor Seidel
bio: I repair books, letters, and maps while trying to accept that some marks deserve to remain.
description: Viktor restores damaged paper for libraries and private collections. He is patient, quietly funny, and attentive in a way that makes people feel heard rather than examined.

questions.question: What should never be restored completely?
questions.answer: Anything whose wear proves it was loved. Repair should protect a history, not make it pretend nothing happened.

questions.question: Which message deserves handwriting?
questions.answer: The one that would sound rehearsed on a screen. A slower medium makes honesty harder to edit.

clues.description: Eight days before Nora mailed her final letter, Viktor's conservation account purchased dark-green archival wax, adhesive-release solvent, and ten miniature inventory tags. He described them as materials for cataloguing a private library, but no completed inventory was recorded.
clues.developerExplanation: Every purchase has a plausible professional use while reproducing the hidden-letter method as a complete kit.

clues.description: Viktor can lift correction film without tearing paper, soften and reset wax seals, and conceal tracking tags inside valuable bindings. He presents those abilities as ordinary conservation work.
clues.developerExplanation: His occupation uniquely combines the paper, seal, and concealment skills required by the crime.

clues.description: A profile photograph of the workbench belonging to Viktor shows a brass sealing stamp with a crescent-shaped chip. The green wax fragment found beneath the desk of Nora carries the same broken crescent in its impression.
clues.developerExplanation: A unique damaged tool links his workshop directly to the tracked reply.

clues.description: Viktor recalls an old client who brought him letters and asked him to uncover a sentence beneath correction film, then never returned. His appointment ledger identifies her as Amelie Rauch, and the building camera records her final confirmed appearance.
clues.developerExplanation: He reveals the historical contact naturally as a memorable restoration job; external records make it decisive.

redHerrings: Bought the tracker hidden in the seal
lookingFor: A woman who values patience, chooses her words carefully, and has a life rich enough that affection would add to it rather than replace it. I appreciate warmth without performance and curiosity without intrusion.

name: Jonas Mertens
bio: I repair buses, name difficult engines, and cook meals requiring fewer tools than my workshop does.
description: Jonas keeps regional buses running and treats mechanical problems with patient humor. He is grounded, musical, and surprisingly enthusiastic about recipes that can survive an interrupted evening.

questions.question: Which machine has the most personality?
questions.answer: The one that behaves perfectly for everybody except the person responsible for repairing it.

questions.question: What song improves a difficult job?
questions.answer: Anything with a steady rhythm and no lyrics confident enough to compete with my swearing.

clues.description: At 22:11, a diagnostic tablet assigned to Jonas passed Nora's building aboard a municipal service bus. Depot cameras show Jonas still repairing another vehicle while the night foreman drove the bus carrying his forgotten tool case.
clues.developerExplanation: The work device creates a false location ping while video separates Jonas from it.

clues.description: Jonas services the buses running through the district where Nora lived and uses Bluetooth diagnostic tools capable of appearing in nearby device scans. He does not work with independent location trackers.
clues.developerExplanation: His technical footprint resembles the tracking clue without matching its purpose or hardware.

clues.description: A road photograph shows the service bus outside the building where Nora lived shortly after her call. A depot time-lapse simultaneously records Jonas beneath a different bus with two coworkers.
clues.developerExplanation: The vehicle is relevant but the mechanic did not accompany it.

clues.description: Jonas jokes about making a night foreman return a diagnostic tablet left on a service bus. Depot video, driver assignment, and tool synchronization all support the story.
clues.developerExplanation: The conversation resolves the device location through three ordinary workplace records.

redHerrings: Maintained the bus used that night
Depot camera keeps him at work
lookingFor: A woman who enjoys quiet evenings, speaks honestly, and does not treat silence as a problem requiring immediate repair. Music and cooking together would be welcome bonuses.

name: Sebastian Blum
bio: I photograph quiet places and people who forget to perform when they think the session is finished.
description: Sebastian produces portraits and small documentary projects for community organisations. He is observant, unhurried, and more interested in why people keep photographs than whether every image is technically perfect.

questions.question: When does a portrait feel truthful?
questions.answer: When the person recognizes herself without feeling reduced to the expression the camera happened to catch.

questions.question: Which photograph would you keep forever?
questions.answer: A slightly blurred kitchen picture where everyone I love is talking at once and nobody noticed the camera.

clues.description: Sebastian's archive contains the last formal portrait taken of Amelie, created for the original Letters First campaign twelve days before she vanished. The complete commission folder includes consent forms, invoices, and every unedited frame.
clues.developerExplanation: The close historical link is fully documented as paid promotional work.

clues.description: Sebastian photographed participants in the earlier letter programme and retained its negatives under his standard archive policy. He was never given participant correspondence or forwarding data.
clues.developerExplanation: He knew Amelie visually but lacked access to her letters and later movements.

clues.description: One profile image uses the same studio backdrop visible behind Amelie in her campaign portrait. The session ledger records separate appointments and identifies all staff present.
clues.developerExplanation: The matching setting reflects the same photographer, not a private meeting.

clues.description: Sebastian remembers his first paid campaign featuring people writing anonymous letters and describes preserving every consent form after a client company closed. The archive index confirms the assignment.
clues.developerExplanation: His conversation explains why the old portrait survived and provides accountable provenance.

redHerrings: Consent form dates the portrait session
lookingFor: A woman who is expressive, direct, and comfortable having interests that do not photograph neatly. I like slow coffee, spontaneous drives, and people who remain curious after first impressions.

name: Matthias Kern
bio: I preserve official records and keep losing the receipts that would make my own life easier to document.
description: Matthias manages historical municipal files and helps residents navigate records written for systems rather than people. He is thoughtful, bookish, and happiest in gardens where nothing requires a reference number.

questions.question: Which record would you save from a fire?
questions.answer: The ordinary neighborhood photographs. Famous buildings survive in books; everyday streets disappear quietly.

questions.question: What deserves to remain private?
questions.answer: Anything preserved for care rather than permission. Access and entitlement are not the same thing.

clues.description: At 20:41, Matthias opened the restricted municipal files for both Klara Weiss and Amelie Rauch. The access fulfilled two separate archive requests submitted by Nils, with each scanned page automatically watermarked and delivered to the journalist.
clues.developerExplanation: He accessed both cases but did so through logged, supervised archive work for another identified profile.

clues.description: Matthias could read unpublished correspondence stored with both historical files. The material contains no mention of Nora, Letters First, or a relationship between the two women.
clues.developerExplanation: His access provides knowledge of each woman separately but not the concealed serial link.

clues.description: A profile photograph taken in the archive includes both file boxes on a return cart behind Matthias. Checkout slips show they were requested and resealed during the same supervised shift.
clues.developerExplanation: Their proximity is explained by the paired request submitted by the journalist rather than private interest.

clues.description: Matthias describes processing two old files for a journalist and being frustrated that privacy rules prevented him from comparing their contents. Request tickets and delivery receipts support the account.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural archive story shows why simultaneous access did not reveal the hidden relationship.

lookingFor: A woman who has strong opinions, treats privacy as a form of respect, and can enjoy an afternoon where very little happens. Books, gardens, and long walks would fit easily.

name: Adrian Koch
bio: I stay calm on the phone and become helpless in front of a long menu.
description: Adrian is composed without being distant. He cooks to unwind after late shifts, runs without tracking his pace, and remembers the small details people mention when they are nervous.

questions.question: What is your favorite kind of quiet?
questions.answer: The first ten minutes after a busy room finally empties.

questions.question: Which decision takes you far too long?
questions.answer: Choosing dinner. I can make urgent choices all night and still lose to a twelve-page menu.

clues.description: At 1:11 a.m., an old dispatcher credential issued to Adrian authenticated with the warning-relay directory. The request came from the city's automated continuity server, but its abbreviated audit does not show which relay command followed.
clues.developerExplanation: Adrian is a principal false lead: his former credential appears at the critical system, while the initial log cannot yet separate an automated test from an outgoing command.

clues.description: Adrian once served as the dispatch centre liaison for overnight relay-continuity tests. His role explains why the old account still exists, although the account should have been archived two years earlier.
clues.developerExplanation: His public work history sustains suspicion without giving him physical access to the abandoned station.

clues.description: A badge visible in an old profile photograph carries the same dispatcher number recorded by the relay. The original image predates the account retirement, and its access stripe is visibly clipped.
clues.developerExplanation: The photograph identifies the credential but also shows that Adrian surrendered the physical badge.

clues.description: Adrian remembers an automated continuity alert interrupting his dinner during the night shift. Dispatch audio, workstation capture, and a meal-delivery receipt keep him at the main centre throughout Eva's call.
clues.developerExplanation: The post-chat cross-check closes both the physical and digital gaps in the explanation Adrian gives.

redHerrings: Live dispatch record confirms his shift
lookingFor: A woman who values steadiness, speaks honestly when something bothers her, and can turn a late dinner into the best part of the day. She does not need to share my schedule, but I hope she understands that calm and quiet are not the same thing.

name: Lukas Bender
bio: I teach useful things, collect terrible bicycle routes, and always pack too many sandwiches.
description: Lukas is energetic, practical, and impossible to embarrass during a demonstration. Away from his classes, he searches for quiet cycle paths and independent cinemas.

questions.question: Which skill should everyone learn once?
questions.answer: How to help without turning someone else into an audience.

questions.question: What makes an unplanned afternoon work?
questions.answer: A bicycle, somewhere to sit, and enough food to make the wrong road worthwhile.

clues.description: Eleven days before Eva vanished, a class led by Lukas rehearsed a roadside rescue beside the abandoned warning station. The municipal permit, twenty-two student check-ins, and continuous instructor-camera footage cover the exercise.
clues.developerExplanation: The location and staged crash resemble the false call, but the large documented class makes the visit ordinary.

clues.description: The course notes belonging to Lukas teach callers to use a familiar name, a precise landmark, and one clear request during an emergency. The wording comes from a nationally published first-aid curriculum.
clues.developerExplanation: His communication knowledge is relevant but widely taught and publicly sourced.

clues.description: A profile photograph places Lukas beside the warning-station sign with a person lying near the road. The uncropped class image reveals training mats, student observers, and a simulation vest.
clues.developerExplanation: The dramatic image is a transparent training photograph rather than a hidden meeting.

clues.description: Lukas jokes about a student making the roadside simulation uncomfortably convincing. The instructor camera and complete class roster confirm that the exercise ended before sunset.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural recollection matches the independent course records and adds no private connection to Eva.

redHerrings: Taught callers how to sound clear
Class video confirms the full session
lookingFor: A woman who likes learning practical things but does not organize every hour of her life. I am drawn to warmth, directness, and somebody who can laugh when a carefully planned bicycle route ends at a locked gate.

name: Thomas Falk
bio: Old buildings tell the truth through crooked floors. I am trying to become equally straightforward.
description: Thomas is blunt, observant, and kinder than his serious expression suggests. He sketches architectural details on receipts and will cross a city to see a staircase worth complaining about.

questions.question: What makes a building feel welcoming?
questions.answer: Signs that people actually use it: worn steps, coats by the door, and one chair in the wrong place.

questions.question: Which imperfection would you preserve?
questions.answer: A repaired crack that shows someone chose to keep the object instead of replacing it.

clues.description: Five months earlier, Thomas opened the complete floor plans for the abandoned warning station and inspected its sealed service entrance. The heritage-work order records every room entered and both keys returned.
clues.developerExplanation: Thomas knows the building better than most suspects, but his access is old and fully documented.

clues.description: Thomas specializes in obsolete municipal buildings and noted that the warning room could still carry sound through disconnected wall speakers. His report recommended removing the remaining cabling.
clues.developerExplanation: His technical observation explains knowledge of the station without connecting him to the later transmission.

clues.description: A photograph shows Thomas inside the relay chamber holding a ring of station keys. File metadata matches the supervised inspection, and the key tag is stamped RETURNED.
clues.developerExplanation: The photograph looks incriminating in isolation but belongs to the recorded survey.

clues.description: Thomas describes arguing that an abandoned building is never truly disconnected while old wiring remains. His inspection report and signed key receipt confirm both the warning and the end of his access.
clues.developerExplanation: The cross-check verifies his professional concern and the key-return chronology.

redHerrings: Opened plans for the warning station
lookingFor: A woman who prefers sincerity to polish and has a fascination of her own that she could explain for an entire walk. Patience helps; so does an appreciation for old places, strong coffee, and plans that leave room for detours.

name: Nico Rehm
bio: Currently powered by night classes, pocket snacks, and the belief that tomorrow will be less busy.
description: Nico is earnest, attentive, and still surprised by how much paperwork follows every practical lesson. He decompresses with basketball highlights and elaborate breakfasts.

questions.question: What is the most reliable night-shift snack?
questions.answer: A cheese roll eaten before you become desperate enough to trust the vending machine.

questions.question: What small gesture improves a difficult day?
questions.answer: Someone remembering that listening can be more useful than fixing.

clues.description: At 1:24 a.m., a training ambulance assigned to Nico crossed Eva's route toward the warning station. At that moment, his trainee badge and supervised patient chart place him inside a hospital across the city.
clues.developerExplanation: The moving vehicle creates a clear location trace, but Nico was not inside it.

clues.description: Nico recognizes the injuries described during the false roadside call as a standard training scenario. The same scenario appears in the regional trainee handbook used by hundreds of students.
clues.developerExplanation: His medical familiarity is broad and does not explain the private family phrase or the synthetic voice.

clues.description: A dashboard photograph maps the ambulance route past the road where Eva stopped. The image was uploaded by Nico's supervisor, who borrowed the vehicle to collect simulation equipment.
clues.developerExplanation: The route is genuine, while authorship and vehicle assignment separate Nico from it.

clues.description: Nico recalls watching the ambulance icon travel without him while he remained on a supervised hospital rotation. The patient chart, badge scan, and training-room camera support his account.
clues.developerExplanation: Three independent records fix Nico across the city during the call and disappearance.

lookingFor: A woman who is patient with an unfinished schedule, comfortable saying what she needs, and willing to celebrate ordinary victories. I would happily trade breakfast recipes, hiking stories, and one genuinely bad podcast recommendation.

name: Oliver Stein
bio: I find patterns in damaged things and try not to assess the risk of every first date.
description: Oliver is cautious without being cynical. He repairs fountain pens, cooks slowly on Sundays, and asks precise questions because he dislikes pretending to understand.

questions.question: Which detail do you notice before other people?
questions.answer: Whether something was repaired with care or merely made to look untouched.

questions.question: What risk is nearly always worthwhile?
questions.answer: Telling someone the honest version before you have perfected the wording.

clues.description: Oliver's claims account opened the files for all four older deaths now connected to the false calls. Assignment records show that each file reached his review queue only after the woman had died.
clues.developerExplanation: Oliver saw the hidden pattern, but the chronology prevents him from using the files to plan the incidents.

clues.description: Oliver's private review notes quote every final 'I'm coming' message and question whether the accidents share a behavioral trigger. He submitted the concern, but four different insurers declined a joint review.
clues.developerExplanation: His notes demonstrate belated pattern recognition rather than advance knowledge.

clues.description: Four color-coded claim folders appear together behind Oliver in a profile photograph. The scan label dates the photograph to a later legal audit that deliberately grouped the files.
clues.developerExplanation: The grouped files are visually suspicious but were assembled after the final older death.

clues.description: Oliver mentions archived claims that looked connected only after they arrived on the same desk years later. Intake timestamps and read-only access records confirm that he never saw a file before its incident.
clues.developerExplanation: His dating-chat anecdote aligns with the delayed claims chronology and limited permissions.

lookingFor: A woman who notices small efforts, says what she means, and has no interest in manufacturing a flawless first impression. Shared hobbies are optional; kindness, curiosity, and the patience for a very slow Sunday meal are not.

name: Rene Wolf
bio: I volunteer at a technology museum and keep adopting machines older than my parents.
description: Rene is open, inventive, and frequently covered in dust from a restoration project. He balances engineering lectures with football, secondhand electronics, and ambitious weekend plans.

questions.question: Which old object deserves another life?
questions.answer: A radio with a tuning dial. Searching for a station should still feel slightly physical.

questions.question: What makes a volunteer day successful?
questions.answer: Everyone leaves tired, nothing catches fire, and one forgotten object works again.

clues.description: Eight weeks before Eva's call, Rene's phone paired with a cataloguing receiver inside the station relay room. A museum partnership had sent six volunteers to document equipment before removal.
clues.developerExplanation: The device pairing proves Rene entered the technical room but places the access well before the crime within a supervised group.

clues.description: Rene helped power and label the old relay console during the museum survey. The volunteers used a separate portable supply and did not reconnect the building transmission line.
clues.developerExplanation: He handled the hardware but not the live municipal circuit used during the false call.

clues.description: A profile photograph shows Rene touching the same console later found warm. The museum inventory board and five other volunteers appear in the uncropped frame.
clues.developerExplanation: The image is fully accounted for by the restoration survey.

clues.description: Rene enthusiastically describes cataloguing an obsolete warning console that briefly paired with every phone in the room. The museum roster and closing camera record his departure eight weeks earlier.
clues.developerExplanation: His account explains both the pairing and photograph while preserving the later access gap.

redHerrings: Phone paired inside the relay room
lookingFor: A woman who enjoys enthusiasm more than polish and has room for projects that do not work on the first attempt. I would love someone who brings her own interests, challenges my assumptions, and occasionally agrees to an unnecessary day trip.

name: Daniel Kranz
bio: I help nervous people sound like themselves, then forget every useful rule when I like someone.
description: Daniel is polished without seeming rehearsed. He listens closely, remembers personal details, and makes even shy people feel that their stories deserve his full attention.

questions.question: What makes a voice memorable?
questions.answer: The moment it stops performing and sounds meant for exactly one person.

questions.question: Which family tradition would you keep forever?
questions.answer: A slow Sunday breakfast where nobody is allowed to turn being late into an apology.

clues.description: At 12:58 a.m., Daniel's coaching laptop created an encrypted synthetic-voice package using the same uncommon model settings as the false Mia recording. His business privacy vault hides the client name and source audio.
clues.developerExplanation: The initial trace is serious but incomplete: matching settings establish capability without yet identifying the modeled voice or relay destination.

clues.description: Daniel previously designed language for municipal crisis simulations. A published workshop slide argues that a private familiar phrase moves people faster than an official warning, combining the exact principles used against Eva.
clues.developerExplanation: His old work connects the psychological method to the emergency system while remaining defensible as professional expertise.

clues.description: Reflected in the glass behind Daniel is a portable WR-9 municipal relay terminal. Its serial number was assigned to him during a former city contract and later declared destroyed instead of being returned.
clues.developerExplanation: The unique serial proves Daniel secretly retained the physical device capable of sending the concealed call.

clues.description: Daniel says the words people obey are ordinary words belonging to one relationship. The platform abuse-recovery cache finds that wording in his deleted chats with the four earlier women and with Eva, who told him: 'Red shoes means my sister needs me without questions.' Device metadata ties his laptop to both scheduled voice models.
clues.developerExplanation: The post-chat comparison supplies the private phrase, repeat-victim pattern, voice-model authorship, and intent that no innocent explanation can unite.

redHerrings: Kept access to the warning relay
lookingFor: A woman who cares about the meaning behind ordinary rituals and is comfortable letting trust develop slowly. I admire independence, emotional generosity, and somebody who can make an imperfect conversation feel more valuable than a polished performance.

name: Felix Moser
bio: I inspect alarms for a living and still jump when my toaster finishes unexpectedly.
description: Felix is practical, warm, and incapable of ignoring a crooked smoke detector. He grows herbs on a narrow balcony and takes pride in repairing things before replacing them.

questions.question: Which household sound always gets your attention?
questions.answer: The smoke alarm, followed closely by the silence after the washing machine should have started.

questions.question: What routine reliably settles you?
questions.answer: Watering herbs after work and checking only once that I locked the door.

clues.description: At 4:40 p.m. on the previous day, Felix used a fire-safety badge to restore power to the warning station switchboard. His work order covered emergency lighting, not the separately fused relay circuit.
clues.developerExplanation: Power access near the crime is suspicious, but circuit separation limits what his authorized task could activate.

clues.description: Felix tested the station speakers by sending a standard evacuation tone through the building wiring. The test unit could play local audio but had no telephone or municipal-network connection.
clues.developerExplanation: He made the speakers audible without possessing the system needed to place the fake call.

clues.description: A photograph shows Felix beside the live switchboard with the relay-room indicator illuminated. The indicator marks backup lighting; the numbered network lockout seal remains visible and intact.
clues.developerExplanation: The misleading indicator is explained by the circuit diagram and preserved seal.

clues.description: Felix recalls a job where an abandoned building became noisy again after years of silence. Coworker video, the electrical invoice, and the unbroken numbered lockout seal confirm he never energized the relay network.
clues.developerExplanation: The conversation cross-check verifies the exact limits of his station work.

redHerrings: Restored power at the warning station
lookingFor: A woman who communicates directly, laughs easily, and understands that competence can coexist with ridiculous habits. I would enjoy sharing recipes, live music, and a home full of plants neither of us pretends to control completely.

name: Johann Adler
bio: I speak to thousands of people after midnight and still rehearse ordering pizza.
description: Johann is charismatic behind a microphone and charmingly hesitant away from one. He collects live recordings, cooks while listening to old soul albums, and dislikes conversations that feel like interviews.

questions.question: Which song deserves a perfect opening?
questions.answer: Any song someone once played for you with unreasonable confidence.

questions.question: When does silence feel comfortable?
questions.answer: When neither person is searching for a performance to fill it.

clues.description: Johann's radio workstation stores the exact thirteen-second birthday video used to model Mia's voice. A station submission record shows Mia uploaded it months earlier, but the initial archive log does not identify who reopened the clip three days before Eva's call.
clues.developerExplanation: Johann is the audio-capability false lead: he holds the exact source recording and professional tools, while authorship remains unresolved initially.

clues.description: Johann produces a listener feature built from family recordings and uses professional voice-repair and cloning software to reconstruct damaged words. Station rules allow synthetic edits only after written consent.
clues.developerExplanation: His ordinary work gives him convincing means without private knowledge of the sisters or access to the warning relay.

clues.description: A monitor behind Johann displays Mia's video beside an open synthetic-speech timeline. The complete project file identifies a station ident voiced by an actor; Mia's clip sits unopened in the adjacent submission queue.
clues.developerExplanation: The cropped photograph merges unrelated windows into a powerful but ultimately false visual connection.

clues.description: Johann describes the sibling-story feature and remembers the producer opening an old birthday submission while he was live on air. The upload history, producer login, and complete overnight broadcast keep Johann away from the modeling workstation.
clues.developerExplanation: Post-chat records explain the source clip, editing screen, and critical access by another employee without connecting either to Daniel.

lookingFor: A woman who enjoys conversation without treating every pause as a problem. She should have music she refuses to apologize for, opinions of her own, and enough spontaneity to turn a late meal into a small occasion.

name: Simon Bruck
bio: I build notifications, ignore half of mine, and take cooperative board games far too seriously.
description: Simon is analytical, playful, and refreshingly willing to admit when he has built something badly. He experiments with vegetarian recipes and organizes game nights that never begin on time.

questions.question: Which notification are you happy to receive?
questions.answer: The message that someone arrived safely, especially when they remembered without being asked.

questions.question: What makes a cooperative game enjoyable?
questions.answer: A team that can lose without turning the rulebook into a court document.

clues.description: At 10:06 p.m., a service account maintained by Simon exported Eva's dating-platform voice-message cache. The same automated backup encrypted 8,412 user archives and recorded no individual playback.
clues.developerExplanation: Simon appears in the handling chain for Eva audio, but the bulk process neither exposed nor selected her recordings.

clues.description: Simon helped build the platform recovery service that preserves deleted voice messages for abuse investigations. Production access requires two approvals that his developer account cannot issue.
clues.developerExplanation: His technical role explains the export infrastructure while separating him from decrypted content.

clues.description: A server dashboard visible in Simon's profile photograph includes Eva's archive number. The image documents a test environment populated with anonymized production-shaped identifiers, not user audio.
clues.developerExplanation: The identifier resembles the live record but belongs to a non-readable interface demonstration.

clues.description: Simon complains about a nightly backup that once made thousands of phones appear active at once. The server audit confirms a bulk encrypted export with no decryption request, search, or audio playback from his account.
clues.developerExplanation: The natural work anecdote and server records explain every digital trace without granting Simon the private phrase.

lookingFor: A woman who is playful without playing emotional games, enthusiastic about something entirely her own, and happy with plans that improve as they go wrong. A competitive streak is welcome if we can still share dinner afterward.

name: Elias König
bio: I preserve old paper for work and make uneven pottery to remember that not everything needs straight edges.
description: Elias is patient, quietly funny, and happiest when a task rewards care instead of speed. He swims before work, listens to jazz while cooking, and gives handmade cups even when their handles are questionable.

questions.question: What deserves more patience than it usually receives?
questions.answer: Learning a craft badly enough to enjoy it before trying to become good.

questions.question: Which routine keeps your week balanced?
questions.answer: An early swim followed by coffee from a cup that leans slightly to the left.

clues.description: At 11:43 p.m., the archive preservation system printed a replacement seal for the box containing the 2003 file. The request used Elias's master account, but its device field identifies an automated scanner batch and does not show whether anyone collected the seal.
clues.developerExplanation: Elias is the archive access false lead. The master account and critical timing deserve attention, while the printer record remains incomplete before conversation.

clues.description: Elias supervises sealed historical boxes and can authorize replacement labels when old paper tears. His access includes the 2003 file, the seal printer, and the conservation room beside aisle seven.
clues.developerExplanation: His legitimate authority gives him opportunity but does not explain the altered report or missing camera minutes.

clues.description: A profile photograph shows Elias holding the 2003 box while a fresh seal rests on the printer tray behind him. Image metadata places the photograph during the afternoon digitization session.
clues.developerExplanation: The image confirms direct handling on the day of the murder, but it predates the unauthorized pencil writing.

clues.description: Elias remembers an automated scanner printing extra seals under his name while he remained at a fixed conservation bench. Continuous bench video, two trainee logs, and the uncollected printer tray confirm his account through the camera gap.
clues.developerExplanation: The unlocked cross-check resolves the apparent seal request and keeps Elias away from aisle seven.

redHerrings: Master account reprinted the box seal
Bench camera confirms his full shift
lookingFor: A woman who values patience, notices quiet effort, and has something she enjoys without needing to master it. I would happily share slow dinners, imperfect handmade objects, and mornings where neither person feels required to entertain the other.

name: Marcel Hartl
bio: I draw details people struggle to describe and spend weekends sketching dogs that refuse to sit still.
description: Marcel is observant, expressive, and careful about separating a person from their worst memory. He collects graphic novels, experiments with ramen, and fills notebooks during train journeys.

questions.question: What is hardest to capture in a drawing?
questions.answer: The way somebody holds themselves when they think nobody is paying attention.

questions.question: Where do you do your best people watching?
questions.answer: On slow trains, where everyone briefly shares a room without needing an introduction.

clues.description: Marcel's illustration archive contains reconstructions of all five historical scenes, including a woman with red thread around her wrist. Each source packet was delivered after the related modern death had already been reported.
clues.developerExplanation: The images look prophetic when grouped together, but their source dates show Marcel illustrated known details rather than planning them.

clues.description: Marcel created scene illustrations for a documentary about The Revisionist. His commission required him to combine damaged archive photographs with written descriptions supplied by the research consultant.
clues.developerExplanation: His job explains accurate visual details and points to an outside source for the historical claims.

clues.description: A spool of red thread and a wrist study appear on the desk in a profile photograph. The uncropped image shows an art reference board and a dated documentary brief.
clues.developerExplanation: The thread is a drawing prop tied to documented production work.

clues.description: Marcel describes receiving unsettling reconstruction briefs only after news reports made the scenes public. Delivery timestamps and layered drawing files confirm when every requested detail reached him.
clues.developerExplanation: The natural work account and file history clear Marcel of advance knowledge.

lookingFor: A woman who is curious about how other people see the world and does not mistake sensitivity for seriousness. I like strong opinions, spontaneous sketches, and anyone willing to judge a new ramen place with unreasonable attention.

name: Boris Seidel
bio: I organize thousands of boxes professionally and still misplace my own keys twice a week.
description: Boris is methodical at work and cheerfully untidy everywhere else. He enjoys woodworking, long hill walks, logic puzzles, and recipes that require one dependable pan.

questions.question: What do you always know where to find?
questions.answer: My wood plane. Everything else is allowed to move when I am not watching.

questions.question: Which puzzle do you refuse to solve quickly?
questions.answer: A difficult route on a paper map, preferably with somewhere warm waiting at the end.

clues.description: Two weeks before Leona died, Boris reprinted barcodes and seals for the aisle containing the five historical files. A water leak had damaged eighty-three labels, and the printer ledger records the full numbered replacement run.
clues.developerExplanation: Broad relabeling access creates opportunity, but the scale and serial record make a secret extra label difficult to hide.

clues.description: Boris designed the box tracking rules and knows that older containers do not record each paper folder separately. His written audit had already recommended correcting that weakness.
clues.developerExplanation: He understands the loophole but documented it before the modern pattern was known.

clues.description: Several unused archive seals appear in a workshop photograph belonging to Boris. Enlarged serial numbers place every seal inside the humidity repair batch later returned to locked storage.
clues.developerExplanation: The photograph shows controlled supplies rather than an unrecorded replacement.

clues.description: Boris jokes about spending a week replacing labels after a leaking pipe ruined the aisle system. The printer ledger, return count, and two-person storage log account for every barcode and seal.
clues.developerExplanation: The cross-check verifies the ordinary repair and closes the spare-label possibility.

redHerrings: Printer ledger accounts for every label
lookingFor: A woman who is dependable without scheduling every pleasant surprise. I admire practical kindness, curiosity, and somebody who can enjoy a long walk even when the chosen route proves less clever than expected.

name: Nando Wolf
bio: I work while the city sleeps and know exactly which chair offers the best view of the moon.
description: Nando is soft spoken, witty, and more social than his schedule suggests. He reads poetry on tram rides, follows amateur astronomy, and treats tea as an evening plan rather than a drink.

questions.question: What improves when everyone else is asleep?
questions.answer: A familiar building. At night you finally hear all the small sounds it makes.

questions.question: Which view is worth staying awake for?
questions.answer: The moon between ordinary rooftops, especially when nobody planned to notice it.

clues.description: Nando's night-desk session went inactive during the same four minutes missing from the archive camera. His library staff card moved to the west map room, where a patron had triggered a locked-door alert.
clues.developerExplanation: The time gap is exact, but a separate tracking system supplies a plausible reason for leaving the desk.

clues.description: Nando can enter the shared reading floor after midnight but has no key for the compact archive shelves. His access ends at the glass divider outside aisle seven.
clues.developerExplanation: His night presence gives proximity without access to the murder aisle.

clues.description: A photograph shows Nando in the archive service corridor after closing. The event badge and wall display date it to a public overnight reading held seven months earlier.
clues.developerExplanation: The image is genuine but unrelated to the murder night.

clues.description: Nando remembers leaving his desk to free a visitor who pushed the wrong map-room door. The patron statement, staff-card trail, and checkout receipt account for all four missing minutes.
clues.developerExplanation: Independent records explain the precise absence that made him suspicious.

redHerrings: Worked beside the archive at night
Staff-card trail follows a lost patron
lookingFor: A woman who enjoys thoughtful conversation, protects time for her own interests, and does not need every evening to be loud. Shared books are welcome, but I care more about warmth, humor, and comfortable silence.

name: Rainer Koch
bio: I type quickly, bake slowly, and believe every kitchen deserves music before breakfast.
description: Rainer is precise, traditional in a comforting way, and happiest when hosting a small table. He practices shorthand for pleasure, listens to classical piano, and plans train trips around bakeries.

questions.question: What should never be rushed?
questions.answer: Bread, apologies, and deciding whether a quiet person has nothing to say.

questions.question: Which old habit would you defend?
questions.answer: Writing directions on paper before a journey, even when my phone already knows the route.

clues.description: At 10:18 p.m. on the murder night, Rainer digitized his legal carbon copy of the original 2003 court transcript. The bound copy contains details omitted from the archive summary, including the fingerprint left on the shelf handle.
clues.developerExplanation: Rainer possesses unpublished knowledge and acts at a suspicious time, but his lawful home copy preserves rather than changes the old account.

clues.description: Rainer typed several hearings connected to the 2003 investigation and retained the permitted reporter copy. Page numbers, court stamps, and binding thread have remained continuous since 2003.
clues.developerExplanation: His access to original testimony is documented and physically stable.

clues.description: The 2003 transcript lies open behind Rainer in a profile photograph. A courier label beside it shows that his memoir editor requested the scan three weeks before Leona began the overnight shift.
clues.developerExplanation: The photo explains the recent digitization and its timing without placing the copy in the archive.

clues.description: Rainer discusses scanning old work notebooks after discovering how much memory had softened their mistakes. Home scanner history and the bound page sequence confirm his copy never entered aisle seven.
clues.developerExplanation: His dating-chat reflection matches the intact legal record and remote location.

redHerrings: Knew details missing from the archive
Legal copy never entered aisle seven
lookingFor: A woman who appreciates consistency but still brings new ideas to the table. I am drawn to emotional honesty, independent interests, and someone willing to spend a slow morning making food without treating the result as a competition.

name: Adrian Falk
bio: I watch priceless objects all week and become far too competitive over completely worthless trivia.
description: Adrian is alert, outgoing, and good at making unfamiliar rooms feel relaxed. He boxes recreationally, photographs quiet streets, and hosts trivia nights where enthusiasm counts more than accuracy.

questions.question: What harmless subject makes you competitive?
questions.answer: City trivia, especially questions I answer confidently and incorrectly.

questions.question: Which moment is worth photographing?
questions.answer: The minute after an event ends, when everyone stops arranging themselves for the camera.

clues.description: The archive security console switched to Adrian's shared guard login during the four-minute camera gap. At the same time, his body camera records him responding to a motion alarm in the museum annex across the courtyard.
clues.developerExplanation: The login creates direct technical suspicion, while body footage places the named guard away from the archive feed.

clues.description: Adrian trained on the archive security layout and can identify two camera blind routes used during maintenance. His badge opens the monitoring office but not the compact shelf room.
clues.developerExplanation: He knows how surveillance works without possessing the physical aisle key.

clues.description: A security map visible in a profile photograph marks the same blind route used to approach aisle seven. The map belongs to a mandatory joint evacuation exercise attended by thirty staff members.
clues.developerExplanation: The route knowledge was shared broadly through required training.

clues.description: Adrian remembers the console falling back to the shared login while he checked an annex alarm. Uninterrupted body-camera footage and the alarm sensor show his entire route during the missing archive video.
clues.developerExplanation: The cross-check separates Adrian from both the console and aisle at the critical time.

redHerrings: Security login covered the camera gap
Body camera records the alarm response
lookingFor: A woman who can laugh at confident mistakes, has a competitive side without making everything serious, and enjoys exploring familiar streets as if they were new. I value direct affection and people who show up consistently.

name: Victor Mader
bio: I recover forgotten local stories and can lose an afternoon inside one footnote.
description: Victor is articulate, attentive, and gifted at making obscure history feel personal. He remembers what people tell him, asks careful questions, and prefers small book fairs to crowded events.

questions.question: What makes an old story feel close?
questions.answer: One ordinary detail that could still happen at your own table today.

questions.question: Which habit do you quietly admire?
questions.answer: Keeping notes for yourself, even when nobody else is expected to read them.

clues.description: Victor's private research index opened all five selected historical summaries shortly before he published each modern connection. Two searches began before the matching crime details were public, although Victor claims he received private early notes from reporters.
clues.developerExplanation: The timing makes Victor a fair initial candidate, but a possible professional source prevents the trace from proving advance planning on its own.

clues.description: Victor's celebrated articles repeatedly call the modern scenes cleaner versions of historical crimes. Archive records also show that he requested neighboring research boxes whose paper folders could conceal one of the supposedly unopened files.
clues.developerExplanation: His language, access pattern, and knowledge align with the method while retaining a surface explanation as research work.

clues.description: A high-resolution profile photograph shows the original paper index card from the 2003 file beneath Victor's notebook. The card was photographed nine days before Leona died, and its torn corner fits a fragment still inside the sealed archive box.
clues.developerExplanation: The physical match proves Victor secretly removed an item from a file the digital system says he never opened.

A recovered draft-history folder on his laptop contains the paragraphs later inserted into all five historical files. Several drafts predate the corresponding murders. The folder also contains Owen's four-minute camera export and a playback sequence matching the archive loop.

redHerrings: Wrote the past to match his crimes
lookingFor: A woman who enjoys following an idea beyond the obvious answer and still knows when to leave work behind. I admire warmth, independence, and someone who values private conversations more than public performance.

name: Owen Brandt
bio: I remove hours from films for a living and cannot shorten a story about a good meal.
description: Owen is expressive, curious, and always aware of how framing changes a story. He collects film scores, experiments with regional recipes, and enjoys screenings where people argue afterward.

questions.question: Which part of a story should never be cut?
questions.answer: The quiet moment that explains why somebody made the loud decision.

questions.question: What makes a film worth discussing afterward?
questions.answer: A choice that still looks different when another person explains what they saw.

clues.description: At 10:47 p.m., Owen's documentary account downloaded the exact four minutes later missing from the archive camera. The request was labeled NIGHT ARCHIVE BACKGROUND, but the initial security report cannot determine whether the export replaced the live feed.
clues.developerExplanation: Owen is the camera and image false lead. He possesses the exact footage used in the loop and works with reconstructed scenes.

clues.description: Owen edited a documentary containing visual recreations of all five historical scenes. Victor served as its research consultant and supplied descriptions that were not visible in the surviving archive photographs.
clues.developerExplanation: His project unites the manipulated imagery and Victor, but editing work can still explain the files on his equipment.

clues.description: A monitor behind Owen shows a red-thread reconstruction beside an archive camera timeline. Project metadata identifies separate documentary sequences placed next to each other during an editing review.
clues.developerExplanation: The cropped screen suggests one operation even though the project file records two unrelated tasks.

clues.description: Owen explains downloading the four-minute clip for quiet hallway footage while the original remained on the archive server. clues.developerExplanation: The post-chat checks clear Owen and show how Victor obtained the exact loop material.

lookingFor: A woman who can disagree without turning the evening into a contest and who brings stories from a world different from mine. I like curiosity, generous humor, and meals that continue long after everyone has finished eating.

name: Hugo Rehm
bio: I study ordinary lives from old records and search flea markets for objects with no practical purpose.
description: Hugo is enthusiastic, talkative, and willing to change his mind when shown a better source. He cycles everywhere, collects old postcards, and treats a flea-market morning as a serious expedition.

questions.question: Which object would you rescue from a flea market?
questions.answer: A postcard with half a conversation and no explanation of how it ended.

questions.question: What changes your mind most effectively?
questions.answer: A specific example offered without making me feel foolish for missing it.

clues.description: At 11:28 p.m., Hugo checked out a numbered archival pencil matching the color and width of the fresh writing in the 2003 file. He reported it missing before leaving the public reading room.
clues.developerExplanation: A missing matching pencil is tangible suspicion, but its location and use remain open before the later checks.

clues.description: Hugo studied copies of three selected historical files and filled their margins with pencil notes. Reading-room rules gave him watermarked copies while the original folders remained behind glass.
clues.developerExplanation: His annotations resemble the alteration process but never touched original pages.

clues.description: A profile photograph shows Hugo holding the numbered pencil beside a copy of the 2003 report. The page carries a large COPY watermark hidden by his hand in the crop.
clues.developerExplanation: The fuller image identifies a permitted study copy, not the altered original.

clues.description: Hugo admits losing a borrowed pencil beneath a reading-room table. Cleaning photographs show it there at 12:03 a.m., while continuous desk video records every copy he annotated and returned.
clues.developerExplanation: The cross-check locates the pencil during Leona murder and accounts for all handled pages.

redHerrings: Made notes on copies of old files
lookingFor: A woman who is enthusiastic about her own interests and comfortable changing plans when something better appears. I value curiosity, emotional openness, and anyone who can spend a morning browsing without needing to buy the sensible object.

name: Samuel Adler
bio: Retirement has given me time for birds, old jazz, and discovering how often my younger self was certain too quickly.
description: Samuel is reflective, direct, and comfortable admitting that experience does not prevent mistakes. He watches birds near the river, cooks for friends, and keeps handwritten notebooks because memory improves its own stories.

questions.question: What becomes easier with age?
questions.answer: Saying I was wrong before the conversation spends an hour proving it for me.

questions.question: Which morning is worth waking early for?
questions.answer: A quiet river, a flask of coffee, and the possibility of seeing one unfamiliar bird.

clues.description: At 9:34 p.m. on the murder night, Samuel scanned his original notebook from the 2003 investigation. It records the bare wrist and fingerprint mistake that were missing from Victor's later article.
clues.developerExplanation: Samuel holds unpublished details at a suspicious time, but the old bound notebook preserves the unaltered history that challenges the killer.

clues.description: Samuel interviewed witnesses in 2003 and openly criticized his own failure to follow the shelf fingerprint. His retirement notes preserve dates, signatures, and photographs excluded from the shortened archive summary.
clues.developerExplanation: His knowledge comes from documented original work and supports the authentic version of events.

clues.description: A profile photograph shows the 2003 notebook open to a drawing of the shelf handle. Binding wear and an old coffee stain continue across both pages, preventing a recent insertion.
clues.developerExplanation: Physical continuity supports the age and authenticity of the notebook.

clues.description: Samuel says retirement prompted him to compare old notebooks with the kinder version preserved by memory. Scan history and continuous page numbering verify that his notes have not changed since 2003.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural reflection explains the recent scan and preserves a reliable control copy of the old scene.

redHerrings: Old notes preserve the untouched version
lookingFor: A woman who has built a life of her own and wants companionship without losing its shape. I value honesty, patient humor, and someone who would enjoy a quiet morning as much as a table full of friends.

name: Jonas Keller
bio: I study why people remember the same moment differently and spend weekends making overly serious pancakes.
description: Jonas is curious without being pushy and has a dry sense of humor about his academic life. He likes long breakfasts, energetic pub quizzes, and people who are comfortable changing their minds.
intent: Hoping for curiosity and easy laughter

questions.question: What ordinary thing do you remember unusually well?
questions.answer: The smell of my grandmother's hallway after rain, even though I could not describe the wallpaper.

questions.question: What is your ideal unplanned evening?
questions.answer: A walk that becomes dinner because neither person is ready to go home yet.

clues.developerExplanation: Jonas created the method and therefore belongs in the shortlist, but the access history shows that someone inside the support organization repeatedly used it.

clues.developerExplanation: His expertise precisely matches the killer's method, making him dangerous-looking without proving that he applied it outside research.

clues.description: A seminar photograph places Jonas beside Alexander at a crisis-communication workshop eleven months ago. The projected slide shows the same seven-step exercise later copied through the support organization's account.
clues.developerExplanation: The image proves that Alexander learned the technique directly while preserving Jonas as a plausible suspect until the conversation cross-check.

Jonas refused, but the shared support account downloaded it the following day. Continuous conference footage places Jonas in Salzburg during Alina's murder.
clues.developerExplanation: The dating conversation reveals a natural work detail. Independent records then clear Jonas and explain how the real killer obtained his method.

lookingFor: A woman who enjoys asking why without needing every conversation to become serious. I value warmth, intellectual honesty, and someone who can laugh when both of us confidently remember the same event differently.

name: Matteo Wolf
bio: I arrange dramatic accidents for a living and avoid unnecessary excitement when I am off the clock.
description: Matteo is disciplined, playful, and far less reckless than his work suggests. He cooks carefully, plans every climbing route twice, and collects terrible action films that ignore all his professional advice.
intent: Looking for something steady off set

questions.question: What harmless skill looks more impressive than it is?
questions.answer: Falling onto a padded mat while keeping hold of a cup of coffee.

questions.question: What makes you trust someone quickly?
questions.answer: They check whether everyone is comfortable before trying to impress the room.

clues.description: Matteo coordinated public-safety reenactments at three locations later used for the murders. His inventory included a reversible dark coat, heavy boots, thin gloves, and a removable left shoe lift matching the seven planted details.
clues.developerExplanation: His work provides the locations, disguise, and physical technique, making him the most visibly threatening innocent suspect.

clues.developerExplanation: The public portfolio explains how another person could study and copy the latest attack without proving Matteo committed it.

redHerrings: Staged attacks at three crime locations
lookingFor: A woman who prefers honest plans to dramatic gestures and understands that careful people can still enjoy adventure. I would like someone affectionate, direct, and willing to disagree about films over a very calm dinner.

name: Lennard Stein
bio: I find missing numbers in complicated claims and lose every argument about where we should order dinner.
description: Lennard is methodical at work but relaxed everywhere else. He restores old furniture, takes slow train journeys without a schedule, and has learned that suspicion is useful in an office but exhausting at home.
intent: Ready to trust life outside work

questions.question: What rule do you happily break?
questions.answer: Dessert can arrive first if both people agree not to pretend it was an accident.

questions.question: How do you recognize a dependable person?
questions.answer: Their small promises receive the same attention as their impressive ones.

clues.description: Lennard searched the addresses, travel histories, and employment records of all four men blamed by the earlier witnesses. Each search occurred through his insurer's investigation system.
clues.developerExplanation: The wide access appears suspicious, but every search follows a documented wrongful-arrest or legal-expense claim.

clues.description: Lennard specializes in finding contradictions between confident statements and objective records. Two falsely accused men publicly thanked him for locating evidence that established their whereabouts.
clues.developerExplanation: His knowledge comes from helping clear suspects rather than creating the statements against them.

clues.description: A desk photograph contains a route map joining three earlier crime streets. File timestamps show that Lennard created it after the third arrest while comparing mileage claims for an appeal.
clues.developerExplanation: The map is visually alarming but has a complete professional history beginning after the crimes.

clues.description: Lennard jokes that his job is finding what people try to hide. Claim assignments, supervisor approvals, and preserved search times show that every case-related lookup began only after an official request. His office entry record covers the latest attack.
clues.developerExplanation: His suspicious phrasing belongs naturally to his profession, while the audit trail removes opportunity and prior knowledge.

lookingFor: A woman who values reliability without expecting perfection. I am drawn to patience, practical kindness, and someone with enough independence to enjoy her own plans while we slowly build shared ones.

name: Levin Roth
bio: My voice works after midnight even when the rest of me is still searching for coffee.
description: Levin is sociable on air and quieter in person. He collects forgotten songs, cooks breakfast at unusual hours, and likes conversations that do not require either person to perform for an audience.
intent: Seeking someone comfortable with odd hours

questions.question: Which song belongs after midnight?
questions.answer: Something slow enough to make an empty street feel intentional rather than lonely.

questions.question: When does silence feel comfortable?
questions.answer: When nobody is rushing to fill it just to prove the evening is going well.

clues.description: Three witnesses regularly listened to Levin's overnight programme. A compressed clip of his voice produces a rough similarity to the calm stranger on Sophie's pocket recording.
clues.developerExplanation: A shared audience and vague voice similarity create suspicion, but neither places Levin with a witness.

clues.description: Levin used the sentence 'I had a clear view' during a broadcast about the first mistaken identification. The episode aired two days after newspapers had already quoted the phrase.
clues.developerExplanation: He repeated public wording rather than originating the phrase.

clues.description: A station photograph shows a dark coat and heavy boots beneath Levin's desk. A wider original image identifies them as a visiting musician's clothing, and both people appear together throughout the broadcast.
clues.developerExplanation: The crop resembles the planted description, while the complete image supplies a documented owner.

clues.description: Levin says his midnight voice reaches rooms he will never see. Uncut studio video and live listener calls place him on air during Alina's attack and all four earlier murders. A clean comparison excludes his voice from Sophie's recording.
clues.developerExplanation: His intimate radio style sounds unsettling out of context, but independent live recordings establish his location and different voice.

redHerrings: Repeated the witness phrase on air
Live studio feeds clear every attack
lookingFor: A woman who does not mind unconventional working hours and prefers sincere conversation to constant entertainment. I appreciate someone with her own passions, a gentle sense of humor, and an excellent breakfast opinion.

name: Benedikt Hahn
bio: I guide drivers through sleeping cities and still take the wrong exit on my days off.
description: Benedikt is calm under pressure and pleasantly unhurried away from work. He enjoys roadside bakeries, restoring bicycles, and choosing scenic routes when nobody is waiting for a delivery.
intent: Looking for a reliable travel companion

questions.question: What makes a journey worth the detour?
questions.answer: A bakery with three tables and somebody who does not mind arriving twenty minutes later.

questions.question: What do you always keep nearby?
questions.answer: A paper map, a bicycle tool, and enough change for coffee from an unreliable machine.

clues.description: Courier vans dispatched by Benedikt crossed camera zones near three murder sites within an hour of the attacks. One passed West Station eleven minutes before Sophie arrived.
clues.developerExplanation: The company operates throughout the city overnight, so broad route overlap is expected rather than unique.

clues.description: Benedikt's route library includes service exits and loading lanes beside all five locations. Delivery restrictions require his company to maintain those maps for overnight drivers.
clues.developerExplanation: His route knowledge has a routine operational explanation and does not show personal travel.

clues.description: A dashboard picture includes West Station's damaged lamp in the distance. Metadata identifies a courier driver's phone rather than Benedikt's device, and the delivery time predates the attack by eleven minutes.
clues.developerExplanation: The image verifies a company route but separates Benedikt and the vehicle from the crime window.

redHerrings: Fleet vans crossed three crime routes
Knew the car park service exits
lookingFor: A woman who enjoys going somewhere without treating every delay as a disaster. I value steadiness, practical humor, and someone whose own ambitions matter as much as the places we might visit together.

name: Oskar Mertens
bio: I remove unnecessary words from serious stories and add unnecessary herbs to every meal.
description: Oskar is direct, thoughtful, and noticeably softer than his professional reputation. He grows herbs on a narrow balcony, reads biographies on trains, and believes a good evening should never feel like an interview.
intent: Interested in an honest second chapter

questions.question: What deserves more attention than it receives?
questions.answer: The person who quietly fixes a problem before everybody else notices it existed.

questions.question: What would your weekend headline say?
questions.answer: Local man ignores telephone, improves soup, reports no regrets.

clues.description: Oskar's newspaper published the detail about the first attacker's left-sided limp twenty-six minutes before police released it. The draft attributes the information to an anonymous encrypted email.
clues.developerExplanation: Early publication gives Oskar apparent prior knowledge, but the preserved message shows that an outside source supplied it.

clues.developerExplanation: The published certainty came from headline policy he opposed, not an attempt to strengthen false accounts.
