redHerrings: Received tips from a hidden sender
lookingFor: A woman who speaks plainly, protects time for herself, and understands that serious work does not require a serious personality at home. Shared meals and mutual respect interest me more than perfect compatibility.

name: Alexander Vogt
bio: I organize neighborhood support visits and believe difficult days become lighter when somebody listens without rushing you.
description: Alexander appears patient, attentive, and quietly dependable. He coordinates community meals, tends a shared garden, remembers small preferences, and makes room for other people without demanding attention for himself.
intent: Looking for gentle and lasting trust

questions.question: What makes someone easy to trust?
questions.answer: Feeling that you can be uncertain without being judged or hurried toward an answer.

questions.question: What do you notice on a difficult day?
questions.answer: Who makes the room feel calmer without making the moment about themselves.

clues.description: Alexander was scheduled for overnight support duty during two earlier attacks. A shared staff tablet viewed nearby incident alerts after both crimes, but shift records do not identify which coordinator used it.
clues.developerExplanation: The timing fairly places Alexander in the shortlist while preserving an ordinary explanation through shared equipment and routine work.

clues.description: Alexander attended Jonas's crisis-communication workshop and later trained volunteers to replace uncertain language with short, confident statements. Four support accounts created under false staff names follow the same seven-question order.
clues.developerExplanation: His training role connects him to the method, but the shared organization still prevents this clue from proving personal use.

clues.description: A high-resolution profile photograph reveals a West Station locker key beside Alexander's bicycle helmet. The unregistered locker contains Matteo's reversible coat, heavy boots, thin gloves, a removable left shoe lift, and fibers matching Alina's clothing.
clues.developerExplanation: The photograph leads to physical evidence connecting Alexander to the planted description and the latest victim.

clues.description: Alexander's calm dating replies prompt uncertain answers without sounding threatening. The cross-check locates an archived support-training video narrated by him. His pronunciation, rhythm, and distinctive pauses match the stranger on Sophie's recording. Device history also ties his personal hotspot to the false support accounts and the anonymous tip sent before the first police release.
clues.developerExplanation: The training audio identifies the helper while the device records, locker contents, and victim fibers provide independent digital and physical proof.

redHerrings: Worked nights during two past attacks
Profile photo exposed the disguise locker
lookingFor: A woman who values kindness without mistaking it for weakness and feels safe admitting when she does not have a perfect answer. I hope for patience, separate interests, and a relationship built through small dependable choices.

name: Emil Bruck
bio: I make performers visible for work and prefer quiet corners when the lights belong to somebody else.
description: Emil is observant, reserved, and unexpectedly enthusiastic about colorful lamps. He visits small concerts, develops photographs at home, and can spend an unreasonable amount of time choosing the atmosphere for dinner.
intent: Looking for a quiet connection with color

questions.question: What makes a room feel welcoming?
questions.answer: Warm light, one comfortable chair, and nobody apologizing for the music they chose.

questions.question: Which color never becomes boring?
questions.answer: Deep blue, because it can make the same place feel peaceful or mysterious.

clues.description: Emil's company serviced lighting at two earlier crime streets and West Station car park. His work account contains diagrams showing exactly where a face becomes difficult to see beneath the damaged lamp.
clues.developerExplanation: His technical knowledge fits the locations, but shared company records do not show personal access during the attacks.

clues.description: Emil publicly demonstrates how changing one lamp can make the same performer appear taller, older, or unfamiliar. A community-safety group attended one demonstration.
clues.developerExplanation: The technique could help disguise an attacker, but it was public and attended by many people.

clues.description: A tool-bench photograph includes the same narrow wrench used to loosen West Station's lamp cover. Serial records show that more than eighty technicians received the identical tool.
clues.developerExplanation: The common equipment cannot identify who damaged the lamp.

clues.description: Emil remarks that the wrong light can make a familiar face look like somebody else. Service logs place him at an arena outside the city during Alina's murder, and lamp-controller history shows the car park light was damaged after his company's final visit.
clues.developerExplanation: His natural professional observation sounds ominous, but timing and controller records clear him.

redHerrings: Worked on lights at two crime scenes
Knew where faces would be hidden
lookingFor: A woman who appreciates quiet confidence, communicates directly, and has a creative interest she could happily discuss for hours. I like affection without pressure and dates where comfortable silence counts as success.

name: Rafael Adler
bio: I clean pauses and background noise from other people's stories, then fill my own kitchen with both.
description: Rafael is expressive, curious, and always listening for sounds other people overlook. He cooks to loud music, collects field recordings while traveling, and prefers imperfect conversation to rehearsed charm.
intent: Hoping to meet someone genuinely expressive

questions.question: What sound makes a place feel like home?
questions.answer: Someone moving around in the kitchen without asking where everything belongs.

questions.question: Which conversation do you replay afterward?
questions.answer: The one where I said something awkward and the other person made it easy to continue.

clues.description: Rafael edited podcast interviews with all four earlier witnesses. Published episodes remove hesitation from their answers, making each person sound more certain than in the police recordings.
clues.developerExplanation: His editing amplified public confidence but occurred after the original statements had already been taken.

clues.description: Rafael advertises his ability to turn broken speech into a clean narrative. Episode notes show that producers specifically asked him to shorten pauses and remove repeated uncertainty.
clues.developerExplanation: The questionable editorial choice came from documented production instructions rather than secret manipulation of witnesses.

clues.description: A studio photograph shows the waveform for the sentence 'I had a clear view.' The source label identifies a copy delivered by police weeks after the first statement, not an original recording made by Rafael.
clues.developerExplanation: He possessed the phrase only after it became part of a licensed podcast episode.

clues.description: Rafael jokes that enough editing can make almost anyone sound certain. The untouched police files contain the complete seven-detail statements before he joined the project, and studio access records place him at work during Alina's attack.
clues.developerExplanation: His profession creates a powerful thematic red herring, but original audio proves that he neither created nor changed the police evidence.

lookingFor: A woman who speaks with enthusiasm, laughs without checking who noticed, and does not expect every pause to be removed. I value emotional honesty, independent plans, and sharing the sounds and places that matter to us.

name: Tobias Seifert
bio: I spent years asking people to choose their words carefully and now mostly negotiate with tomatoes and one stubborn cat.
description: Tobias is measured, self-aware, and enjoying a slower life after the courtroom. He grows vegetables, repairs old clocks, plays patient games of chess, and prefers people who challenge him without trying to win every exchange.

questions.question: Which opinion have you changed with age?
questions.answer: I once thought admitting uncertainty weakened a decision. Now I trust it more than false confidence.

questions.question: How should a slow Sunday begin?
questions.answer: Coffee outside, no timetable, and a newspaper that remains folded for at least an hour.

clues.description: Fourteen years ago, Tobias wrote that a witness 'had a clear view' while upholding a conviction later overturned by new evidence. The falsely accused man died before the court formally cleared him.
clues.developerExplanation: The old ruling supplies a possible origin for the repeated phrase and gives Tobias an alarming connection, but it predates the murders and does not show who later copied it.

clues.description: Tobias now gives public talks about the danger of confident eyewitness accounts. He openly discusses the overturned case and accepts responsibility for trusting certainty over inconsistent physical records.
clues.developerExplanation: His present work addresses his former mistake rather than teaching the killer's private seven-step method.

clues.description: A photograph shows Tobias meeting one of the men falsely accused in the recent murders. The full event album identifies a public legal-reform panel attended by more than two hundred people.
clues.developerExplanation: The meeting is real but public, documented, and focused on preventing mistaken identification.

clues.description: Tobias says some people should never walk away from consequences. His archived judgment proves the repeated phrase existed long before the murders. A family-record cross-check identifies the wrongly convicted man as Alexander's father, while train tickets, event video, and witnesses place Tobias at public concerts during every attack.
clues.developerExplanation: His stern language and past ruling build a believable red herring. The chronology clears Tobias while the newly revealed family link explains Alexander's need to control who witnesses blame.

redHerrings: Used the phrase in an old judgment
lookingFor: A woman who values reflection, keeps her own convictions, and can disagree without turning affection into a contest. I hope for steady companionship, separate passions, and enough humor to prevent either of us becoming too solemn.

name: Clara Neumann
bio: I rescue overlooked objects from storage and occasionally remember to leave the museum.
description: Clara is observant, self-contained, and unexpectedly funny once a conversation stops feeling formal. Her museum recently catalogued the same tableware line as the blue cup found at Oscar's home, giving her detailed knowledge of its age and design. The catalog request and every photographed piece remain documented in the museum collection.
lookingFor: A man who is quietly confident, asks thoughtful questions, and understands that silence can be comfortable. I like people who care about where things came from without treating every old object as precious. Shared museums would be lovely, but warmth matters more than matching hobbies.

questions.question: Which object would you never replace with a newer version?
questions.answer: My grandmother's dented tea tin. It closes badly, looks ordinary, and still makes every kitchen smell like hers.

questions.question: What makes a conversation worth remembering?
questions.answer: When someone notices the small answer hiding behind the confident one.

clues.description: Clara searched the exact blue-and-cream tableware series four times during the month before Oscar died. Each search came from the museum network and is attached to a documented collection audit.
clues.developerExplanation: Clara knows the cup design through legitimate museum work. Her records predate Oscar's match with her and create no link to Mathias or either home.

clues.description: Her profile places unusual value on inherited household objects, but the answer has remained unchanged for three years and refers to her grandmother's tea tin.
clues.developerExplanation: The sentimental-object language resembles the killer's ritual only superficially. Clara's named object and its history are independently documented.

clues.description: A cup from the same product line appears in a museum photograph on Clara's profile. Its inventory number is visible beneath the base, and it has never left the collection.
clues.developerExplanation: The matching design is a fair visual red herring. The inventory mark and museum image archive prove it is not Mathias's cup.

clues.description: Clara speaks naturally about objects carrying memories, then identifies the blue series as common hotel china rather than a handmade piece. Her explanation matches the museum catalog.
clues.developerExplanation: Her conversation reinforces the innocent professional explanation and adds no access to either victim.

name: Mara Vogel
bio: Muddy boots, balcony tomatoes, and breakfast serious enough to require planning.
description: Mara is energetic, direct, and happiest when a plan ends with soil under her nails. A delivery record places her inside Oscar's apartment building the afternoon before his death, and several plants in her cooperative require careful handling. The signed delivery and plant inventory provide ordinary explanations for both details.
lookingFor: A man who can be spontaneous without being unreliable, laughs easily, and says what he means. He does not need to know one herb from another, but he should be willing to cook with whatever survived my balcony that week. Kindness to service staff is non-negotiable.

questions.question: What is your most useful unnecessary skill?
questions.answer: I can tell whether basil is thirsty from across a courtyard. This has impressed nobody so far.

questions.question: What would we cook on a rainy evening?
questions.answer: Something forgiving in one pot, followed by bread that I confidently claim was meant to look rustic.

clues.description: A cooperative delivery logged Mara at Oscar's building one day before the dinner. The recipient signature belongs to the restaurant occupying the ground floor, not to Oscar.
clues.developerExplanation: Mara was physically near Oscar's home, but the time, recipient, and delivery contents are documented. She has no link to Mathias or the cup.

clues.description: Her gardening cooperative grows plants that carry warning labels, but none can produce the toxin identified in Oscar's meal.
clues.developerExplanation: The dangerous-plant assumption is intentionally simple and tempting. A direct substance comparison clears it.

clues.description: A tray in Mara's market photograph resembles Oscar's serving tray. The vendor stamp identifies a common restaurant-supply model sold across the city.
clues.developerExplanation: The object resemblance gives the photo something concrete to inspect without creating a trophy-chain link.

clues.description: Mara says she delivered basil to a restaurant beneath an apartment block and complained about carrying it upstairs by mistake. The address and recipient match the cooperative log.
clues.developerExplanation: The conversation reveals the building overlap through an ordinary dating anecdote and resolves it consistently.

name: Nina Hartl
bio: I know the scenic route, the cheap train, and where both usually go wrong.
description: Nina is independent, articulate, and more interested in how people travel than in collecting destinations. Her assignments placed her in two cities where earlier deaths occurred, and one expense photograph includes a blue cup. Publication dates, rail tickets, and the cup's hotel logo make the overlap traceable rather than secretive.
lookingFor: A man who has a life of his own, listens closely, and treats kindness as a habit rather than a performance. He does not need to love travel, but he should understand why returning somewhere can matter more than seeing somewhere new. I appreciate people who can change plans without changing personality.

questions.question: Which journey would you happily repeat?
questions.answer: The slow train through the Danube valley, preferably with someone who does not call every delay an adventure.

questions.question: What do tourists usually miss?
questions.answer: The places where people buy breakfast before work. A city is most honest before it starts posing.

clues.description: Nina's verified work itinerary passes through the cities of two earlier deaths. Both visits ended before she connected with either man, and rail records place her elsewhere on the relevant nights.
clues.developerExplanation: The geographic overlap sounds broad and suspicious but collapses under simple chronological checking.

clues.description: Nina writes frequently about meals that make unfamiliar places feel like home. The articles are public travel essays and never mention any victim or private kitchen.
clues.developerExplanation: Her writing echoes the killer's comforting language without granting access to the men.

clues.description: A blue cup appears in Nina's breakfast photograph. Its visible hotel crest and image date identify it as commercial china photographed eleven months before Mathias died.
clues.developerExplanation: The photo invites visual comparison but contains its own straightforward exclusion.

clues.description: Nina remembers the blue hotel cup because it leaked coffee onto her notes. Her route, article deadline, and complaint receipt all match the original trip.
clues.developerExplanation: Her distinctive travel story ties all of her apparent clues into one verifiable innocent event.

redHerrings: Writes about meals that feel like home
Blue cup appears in travel photo

name: Sophie Kern
bio: I collect useful noises and lose my headphones in increasingly creative places.
description: Sophie is playful, perceptive, and inclined to remember a room by its sound. A field recording places her near Oscar's street, and Oscar saved one of her voice notes shortly before dinner. The recording slate and production team establish when and why she was there, while the voice note remains ordinary flirting.
lookingFor: A man who is emotionally steady, curious about other lives, and able to laugh when a careful plan changes. I like voices with character, opinions about films, and people who can enjoy a quiet room without reaching for their phone.

questions.question: Which sound instantly improves your mood?
questions.answer: A key turning in my own front door after a long day. Very ordinary, completely undefeated.

questions.question: What would your friends ask me first?
questions.answer: Whether you can tolerate me pausing a film because the rain sounds suspiciously perfect.

clues.description: A recording uploaded by Sophie carries a location tag one street from Oscar's building. Its production slate dates it nine days before his death and names three crew members.
clues.developerExplanation: The location overlap is real but not temporally relevant. It gives Sophie a personalized, verifiable lead.

clues.description: Oscar saved Sophie's voice note under the label 'dinner sound.' The original message is a recording of onions frying for a playful profile exchange.
clues.developerExplanation: A suggestive label is resolved by the harmless source audio.

clues.description: Her equipment photograph includes a folded place setting, but metadata and the prop list link it to a restaurant commercial recorded months earlier.
clues.developerExplanation: The staged dining image is visually relevant while remaining clearly separate from Oscar's home.

clues.description: Sophie recreates the harmless 'dinner sound' joke and names the same field-recording crew found in the file metadata.
clues.developerExplanation: Her conversational detail confirms that the voice note and street recording belong to separate documented moments.

redHerrings: Oscar saved her dinner voice note
Place setting appears in equipment photo

name: Leonie Brandt
bio: Strong coffee, calm hands, and an ongoing negotiation with my sleep schedule.
description: Leonie is warm without being sentimental and direct without being unkind. She asked Oscar whether he took heart medication, recognized the symptoms reported in an earlier death, and worked at the hospital that received Mathias. Those details make her a serious initial suspect, but ward records place her continuously on duty during Oscar's dinner and she has no connection to the transferred objects.
lookingFor: A man who respects boundaries, notices small kindnesses, and can make plans around an imperfect schedule. I value honesty about health, family, and what someone actually has room for. A quiet breakfast after a night shift can be more romantic than an elaborate evening.

questions.question: What does reliability look like to you?
questions.answer: Doing the small thing you promised even after the impressive moment has passed.

questions.question: What should a partner know early?
questions.answer: My schedule is strange, I ask practical questions, and neither means I am uninterested.

clues.description: Leonie asked Oscar about heart medication two days before his death. Her hospital badge then remained inside the emergency ward from 18:43 until 06:12, covering the entire dinner window.
clues.developerExplanation: Leonie is an intended shortlist suspect. Her medical question is alarming, but a strong continuous work record excludes her from the home.

clues.description: Her professional training includes recognizing the symptoms caused by the toxin in Oscar's meal. Thousands of emergency staff share that training, and supply records show no access to the substance itself.
clues.developerExplanation: Knowledge is separated from access. This reinforces the game's rule that competence alone is not proof.

clues.description: A hospital break-room photograph shows blue ceramic mugs, but each bears the hospital crest and none matches the chip pattern of Mathias's cup.
clues.developerExplanation: The color resemblance is deliberately weak and provides no trophy link.

clues.description: Leonie says she asks dates about allergies and medication before cooking because of an emergency involving her father. Her father confirms the event, and her shift account matches the badge log.
clues.developerExplanation: Her intimate health question receives a personal, verifiable explanation in a natural dating conversation.

name: Eva Stein
bio: I make cups slightly too large and tell stories slightly too long.
description: Eva is expressive, tactile, and incapable of discussing a mug without turning it over to inspect the base. She works with a blue glaze resembling the cup at Oscar's scene, sold ceramics near Mathias's district, and once asked Oscar for a photograph of his kitchen shelf. Her maker's mark, sales ledger, and the recovered cup's factory mold separate her work from the evidence.
lookingFor: A man who is warm but independent, comfortable with honest disagreement, and willing to care about how everyday things are made. I would rather hear his real opinion than receive a perfect answer. Bonus points if he has one terrible mug he refuses to throw away.

questions.question: What everyday object deserves better design?
questions.answer: Travel mugs. Most are engineered for a hand belonging to someone much less clumsy than me.

questions.question: What is your favorite kind of gift?
questions.answer: Something useful with one imperfect detail that proves a person chose it rather than ordered it blindly.

clues.description: Eva advertised cups in a blue glaze visually similar to the one found beside Oscar. Her pieces carry a thumb-shaped maker's mark; the recovered cup has a factory number instead.
clues.developerExplanation: Eva is the strongest visual red herring and an intended shortlist choice. The base markings give the player a simple, decisive distinction.

clues.description: Her sales map includes a market three streets from Mathias's home. The ledger lists every buyer from that event, and Mathias is not among them.
clues.developerExplanation: The location overlap supports suspicion without inventing an undocumented sale to the victim.

clues.description: Eva's profile shows six blue cups on a drying shelf. High-resolution metadata reveals her thumb mark beneath every base and dates the batch after Mathias's cup was already missing.
clues.developerExplanation: The photograph looks highly relevant until its manufacturing detail and date are compared.

clues.description: Eva says she asks for shelf photographs before making custom cups so their size and color suit the kitchen. Oscar sent one, but no order or visit followed.
clues.developerExplanation: Her request for Oscar's kitchen image has a businesslike explanation and never places her inside the home.

redHerrings: Makes cups in a matching blue glaze
Asked to see Oscar's kitchen shelf

name: Helena Weiss
bio: I make complicated evenings feel simple and still prefer dinner at a crowded kitchen table.
description: Helena is composed, attentive, and skilled at making other people feel that their preferences were her idea all along. Her profile presents home cooking as warmer than restaurant dates. Nothing in her public manner feels threatening, but a former account on her device reached Mathias, a later photograph contains his missing cup, and her wording matches the private invitation Oscar received.
lookingFor: A man who keeps his word, values the small rituals that make a home feel lived in, and is secure enough to be cared for without turning it into a performance. I notice what people remember about their families. A good meal and an honest story will always impress me more than an expensive room.

questions.question: What makes a home feel welcoming?
questions.answer: Someone remembering how you take your coffee, a table that is allowed to look used, and no pressure to be impressive.

questions.question: What would you bring to a first dinner?
questions.answer: Something small for the table. Wine disappears; a useful object becomes part of the room.

clues.description: A deleted dating profile used on Helena's phone matched Mathias during the week of his death. The account vanished the following morning, but its device token later opened Helena's current profile.
clues.developerExplanation: The device token gives Helena a hidden link to Mathias. The other channels prove that the connection continued into physical possession of his cup and access to Oscar.

clues.description: Helena's profile says she brings a useful object when someone hosts. Oscar's backed-up notification shows that she offered to bring something for his table while asking him to choose a meal from home.
clues.developerExplanation: Her public profile independently describes both parts of Oscar's private dinner invitation: the comforting meal and the object brought for his table.

clues.description: A photograph Helena uploaded six weeks after Mathias died shows the blue cup beside her breakfast. Its chipped rim and uneven cream stripe match the cup later recovered from Oscar's table.
clues.developerExplanation: This establishes Helena's possession of Mathias's cup between the two deaths. No innocent profile connects the exact object to both men.

clues.description: Helena says, 'You choose the meal; I'll bring something for the table.' The sentence exactly matches the surviving preview of Oscar's off-app dinner invitation.
clues.developerExplanation: Helena repeats her invitation ritual naturally while speaking to another possible date. Combined with the device and cup, the phrase identifies her as Oscar's guest.

redHerrings: Mathias's cup appears in her photo

name: Lara König
bio: I design sensible paths and then take the least sensible one home.
description: Lara is measured, outdoorsy, and better at drawing feelings than naming them. Her firm purchased a restricted landscaping chemical and surveyed the courtyard behind Oscar's building. Laboratory comparison excludes the chemical, while the dated plans show that Lara never entered the residential floors.
intent: Interested in a calm, real connection
lookingFor: A man who can enjoy a quiet evening as much as an ambitious day and does not need to fill every silence. I like honest conversation, practical kindness, and people who can disagree without making affection feel conditional.

questions.question: Where do you go when you need to think clearly?
questions.answer: Somewhere with a long path and no expectation that I reach the end of it.

questions.question: What is a green flag nobody mentions?
questions.answer: Someone returning a borrowed thing before you have to ask for it.

clues.description: Lara approved a controlled landscaping chemical for a courtyard project behind Oscar's building. Laboratory comparison finds no component shared with the toxin in his meal.
clues.developerExplanation: Chemical access creates suspicion, but the direct lab mismatch keeps it from competing with the intended shortlist.

clues.description: Her project map includes Oscar's address, but the marked work area is the commercial courtyard and the survey ended two months before his death.
clues.developerExplanation: The map is a real location link with clear spatial and temporal limits.

clues.description: A silver spoon lies beside Lara's field notebook. Enlarging the image shows a folding measuring tool, not dining cutlery.
clues.developerExplanation: The object resembles Oscar's missing spoon only at thumbnail size and resolves through visual inspection.

clues.description: Lara complains that the Oscar-street courtyard project was cancelled before construction. Her description matches the archived plans and contractor notices.
clues.developerExplanation: Her case-adjacent work enters the chat as a believable professional frustration, not an interrogation.

redHerrings: Mapped the courtyard behind Oscar's home
Silver object appears in field photo

name: Amelie Roth
bio: Too many books beside the bed, too many questions before breakfast.
description: Amelie is curious, earnest, and occasionally unaware that an academic question can sound intensely personal. Her research examines how meals and household objects carry memory after bereavement, and Mathias once completed an anonymous university survey. Ethics records show that she never received his identity or address.
lookingFor: A man who is direct without being harsh, affectionate without being possessive, and genuinely interested in the world. I enjoy people who can tell a personal story without turning it into a performance. Shared books help, but emotional honesty matters more.

questions.question: Which ordinary ritual matters more than it should?
questions.answer: Calling my sister while I cook on Thursdays. We run out of news after ten minutes and stay on anyway.

questions.question: What question do you ask too often?
questions.answer: Why people keep one object and discard another. I am learning not to ask it while they are still unpacking.

clues.description: Mathias completed a university survey associated with Amelie's research group. Participant identities were encrypted before Amelie joined the project, and her account never accessed the private key.
clues.developerExplanation: The victim link is real but anonymous. Access logs make the boundary understandable and testable.

clues.description: Her research asks grieving participants about comfort meals and meaningful household objects, closely resembling the killer's questions. The questionnaire has been publicly available for four years.
clues.developerExplanation: Amelie's research could have inspired the method, but it neither identifies victims nor connects her to Oscar's home.

clues.description: A research-board photograph displays pictures of cups and spoons submitted by study participants. Mathias's blue cup is not among the archived images.
clues.developerExplanation: The board visually resembles the trophy pattern, but the underlying dataset excludes the key object.

clues.description: Amelie describes the public survey and admits that asking dates research questions is a bad habit. Her wording matches the published questionnaire rather than Oscar's private invitation.
clues.developerExplanation: Her thematic similarity is exposed as professional curiosity, with no hidden knowledge of the men.

name: Tessa Falk
bio: Numbers behave better than people, but the interesting ones still surprise you.
description: Tessa is dry, practical, and quietly generous with people she trusts. Her account purchased vintage tableware from a seller who once listed Mathias's cup pattern, and hotel invoices include dozens of replacement spoons. The payment trail leads to documented banquet stock rather than either victim's home.
lookingFor: A man who has strong opinions, a generous streak, and enough self-awareness to change his mind. I prefer plans that leave room for a second coffee and people who do not confuse drama with passion. He should have his own interests and ask about mine because he actually wants the answer.

questions.question: Which luxury is actually worth paying for?
questions.answer: A breakfast you did not cook and a checkout time late enough to enjoy it.

questions.question: What do you collect without meaning to?
questions.answer: Receipts from good days. They become bookmarks and then refuse to leave.

clues.description: Tessa authorized a bulk tableware payment to a vintage dealer who once advertised Mathias's cup pattern. The invoice lists forty hotel pieces, none matching the recovered cup.
clues.developerExplanation: The transaction creates a traceable marketplace link but no possession of the trophy.

clues.description: Her hotel replaced engraved serving spoons shortly before Oscar's spoon vanished. Inventory photographs show a different crest, size, and handle pattern.
clues.developerExplanation: The spoon purchase resembles the missing trophy only at the category level.

clues.description: Tessa's market photograph includes a stall selling blue cups. Metadata predates Mathias's death, and the dealer confirms she bought only numbered hotel stock.
clues.developerExplanation: The marketplace photo links her clues visually while its date and receipt exclude the case object.

clues.description: Tessa jokes about buying forty mismatched spoons for a hotel breakfast room. The quantity and engraved crest match the purchase invoice exactly.
clues.developerExplanation: Her conversation gives the bulk purchase a specific, mundane destination and no connection to a private dinner.

redHerrings: Bought from a connected tableware dealer
Blue cups appear in market photo

name: Mila Schubert
bio: I organize a city's forgotten paperwork and keep my own books in cheerful disorder.
description: Mila is thoughtful, understated, and capable of making administrative history unexpectedly funny. She opened archived dispatch records connected to two earlier incidents and copied their timings into a work notebook. The records were part of a documented digitization project begun after both men had died.
lookingFor: A man who is curious without needing to dominate every conversation, keeps small promises, and can enjoy an evening that does not require a plan. I appreciate dry humor, honest questions, and people who return books without being reminded twice.

questions.question: Which small piece of history would you save?
questions.answer: An ordinary letter describing an ordinary day. Important events already have enough people protecting them.

questions.question: What is your most disorganized habit?
questions.answer: I file documents perfectly and leave every kitchen cupboard open like a trail behind me.

clues.description: Mila accessed dispatch reports from two earlier first accidents. Her archive assignment began six months after the later incident and includes 1,840 unrelated emergency records.
clues.developerExplanation: Mila saw the records only through a broad, documented archive project long after the events. She had no access to the men or the original calls.

clues.description: Her work notes preserve exact call and incident times, but the dates and archive references show that she copied them during cataloguing rather than before the accidents.
clues.developerExplanation: The suspiciously precise timings are copied from official records, not advance knowledge.

clues.description: A profile photograph shows boxes labeled EMERGENCY CALLS. The visible archive code matches the public digitization project and not any private case file.
clues.developerExplanation: The image looks ominous until its catalog code is read.

clues.description: Mila describes entering old call times into a public archive database and names the same project code visible in her photograph.
clues.developerExplanation: Her dating conversation supplies a consistent work explanation without knowledge of the current inquiry.

name: Romy Keller
bio: I make excellent coffee, acceptable cakes, and playlists my staff keep trying to replace.
description: Romy is sociable, practical, and happiest when feeding people without making a ceremony of it. Her cafe delivered meals to Paul during recovery, a driver entered his building, and Romy called him near one appointment. Receipts, courier tracking, and the recorded booking explain each contact.
intent: Open to a warm, steady relationship
lookingFor: A man who is kind when nobody is performing for him, communicates directly, and understands that busy weeks do not mean a lack of interest. I like good appetites, bad jokes, and someone willing to stay after closing while I count the chairs.

questions.question: What should every neighborhood have?
questions.answer: One place where you can arrive alone without feeling as if you are waiting for somebody.

questions.question: Which food do you defend too passionately?
questions.answer: Plain butter cake. It does not need fruit, cream, or a marketing strategy.

clues.description: Romy's cafe completed five food deliveries to Paul during his recovery. Every order came through the public delivery service and was left by one of three registered couriers.
clues.developerExplanation: Romy reached Paul through ordinary business transactions, not private caregiving.

clues.description: A cafe driver entered Paul's building twice, but location logs show Romy remained at the cafe during both deliveries and during his first fall.
clues.developerExplanation: The business entered the building while Romy did not.

clues.description: One profile photograph includes the same insulated bag seen outside Paul's apartment. Its numbered courier patch identifies a bag shared by the cafe delivery team.
clues.developerExplanation: The bag belongs to the service, and the tracking record accounts for it.

clues.description: Romy says she called a recovering customer because his regular courier order conflicted with a clinic appointment. The cafe booking log contains the same rescheduling note.
clues.developerExplanation: Her apparently personal call is a documented customer-service exchange.

redHerrings: Sent five meals during Paul's recovery
Called Paul near a clinic appointment

name: Johanna Lind
bio: I keep old buildings standing and lose arguments with the shelves in my own apartment.
description: Johanna is capable, candid, and visibly impatient with unsafe shortcuts. questions.question: Which public place makes you want to stay?
questions.answer: A square with shade, food nearby, and enough different kinds of seats that nobody is forced to use it the same way.

questions.question: When should a plan be changed?
questions.answer: When the people using it behave differently from the people imagined on paper. Reality deserves a vote.

questions.answer: How does that actually work? Pretending to understand is responsible for many terrible exhibitions.

clues.developerExplanation: Her role gave her a legitimate reason to access sealed kits, including the fatal four, but also many harmless ones.

name: Eva Dorn
bio: I build table arrangements for work and come home looking like I lost an argument with a forest.

questions.question: What makes a gift feel personal?
questions.answer: A sign that the person noticed you, not a sign that they spent the most money.

questions.question: Which rule do you never bend at work?
questions.answer: Unknown plants stay labeled and out of reach. Beautiful does not automatically mean harmless.

name: Luisa Quade

questions.question: When is the longer route better?
questions.answer: When the company is good, the view changes, or getting there quickly was never the important part.

questions.question: What do you plan and what do you leave open?
questions.answer: Trains and dinner reservations get planned. The conversation between them should not.

questions.question: What deserves more patience than people usually give it?
questions.answer: Trees, difficult conversations, and anyone trying to learn something in front of other people.

questions.question: What is your favorite kind of bad weather?
questions.answer: Steady rain when I have nowhere urgent to be and shoes that can survive it.

questions.question: What is always worth paying a little more for?

questions.question: Which rule do you follow only reluctantly?

questions.question: Which sound instantly changes your mood?
questions.answer: A train beginning to move while rain is hitting the window.

questions.question: When is silence comfortable?

questions.answer: The undersides of leaves. They are usually stranger and more interesting than the polished side.

questions.question: What unfinished project are you still fond of?

questions.question: What makes an unfamiliar place feel safe?

clues.developerExplanation: Her clients supplied motive and partial knowledge, but she lacked the cross-agency material used in the releases.

clues.description: Dagmar publicly argued that Madam Verdict's disclosures should be preserved as admissible leads, even while condemning the deaths. Critics quoted only the first half of her position.
clues.developerExplanation: She supported using verified information, not the murders, but edited clips made her look like an admirer.

clues.description: Dagmar wears a red V pin in a profile photograph taken at a families' rally. Organizers distributed two thousand identical pins before the symbol became commercial merchandise.
clues.developerExplanation: The pin signals solidarity with harmed families and creates deliberate ambiguity about support for the killer.

clues.description: Dagmar says she stopped believing every powerful man deserves advance warning. She means that families should not alert an opponent before filing for an emergency protective order.
clues.developerExplanation: The reply sounds like killer logic until its ordinary legal context is restored.

redHerrings: Represented families harmed by four men
Wore Madam Verdict's red V at a rally
Said powerful men do not deserve warnings

name: Jule Bernhardt
bio: I make charts for a living but refuse to score dates in spreadsheets. I like midnight bakeries, obscure trivia, and plans with generous error margins.
description: Jule is playful, highly observant, and happiest when turning intimidating numbers into understandable stories. She enjoys being proven wrong when the surprise is interesting.
intent: Looking for curious conversation and real affection
lookingFor: A man who asks good follow-up questions, can laugh at his own predictions, and never treats feelings like a problem to optimize.

questions.question: What would your least useful chart measure?
questions.answer: Confidence before assembling furniture compared with screws left over afterward.

questions.question: Which prediction are you happy to get wrong?
questions.answer: That I will leave a party early and avoid ordering one more plate for the table.

clues.description: The timing headers in all five releases match an automation package Jule helped configure. Sixty-eight political, media, and nonprofit organizations use the same open package.
clues.developerExplanation: She had the skill to schedule the drops, but the technical signature is shared widely and contains none of her private code.

clues.description: Jule's work account searched every man's name before the corresponding public post. Internal briefs show that city analysts received advance warnings and assigned her to model possible public reaction.
clues.developerExplanation: The search timing seems impossible for an outsider until the confidential forecasting assignment is found.

clues.description: A blurred monitor in Jule's profile photo displays a red line labeled V6. The original dashboard identifies it as voter model version six, created months before the sixth verdict announcement.
clues.developerExplanation: The visual coincidence is striking but unrelated when the uncropped dashboard is read.

clues.description: Jule jokes that the right spreadsheet can end a career before lunch. She is describing election forecasts, and archived team chat shows colleagues using the same joke long before the murders.
clues.developerExplanation: The joke is dark enough to draw suspicion while its origin remains ordinary and verifiable.

redHerrings: Her software scheduled every verdict release
Searched each man before the public posts
Modeled how every death changed the election

name: Petra Adler
bio: I argue about housing by day and sing songs far outside my range by night. Market coffee, neighborhood gossip, and unapologetic karaoke keep me balanced.
description: Petra is outspoken, funny, and comfortable taking up space. Her public confidence hides a sentimental attachment to local traditions and handwritten birthday cards.
intent: Looking for chemistry without political theatre
lookingFor: A man who is not intimidated by direct women, has loyalties beyond himself, and can survive a duet performed with more courage than talent.

questions.question: Which song would you sing with too much confidence?
questions.answer: Anything with a final note I cannot reach and will attempt twice anyway.

questions.question: What should every neighborhood protect?
questions.answer: A cheap cafe, an old tree, and at least one person who knows everybody's birthday.

clues.description: Petra's private phone connected near three verdict meeting rooms on the relevant evenings. Council attendance records place her in adjoining public chambers with dozens of witnesses.
clues.developerExplanation: Location data creates a compelling shortlist candidate but does not place her inside the private rooms.

clues.description: Petra's polling and donations rose after every Madam Verdict disclosure. She used the exposed corruption in speeches but consistently called the killings indefensible.
clues.developerExplanation: She benefited politically, yet public benefit is not proof that she created the events.

clues.description: Petra holds a crimson folder labeled V-06 in a profile photograph. The uncropped image shows a transport hearing, where V-06 was the public code for the sixth voting item.
clues.developerExplanation: The color and number imitate the sixth verdict by coincidence, making Petra a strong visual red herring.

clues.description: Petra says the right document can end a career before breakfast. She is discussing a verified committee report, and the report's public filing confirms the context.
clues.developerExplanation: Her boast is politically ruthless but does not imply secret knowledge or physical involvement.

redHerrings: Was near three verdict meeting rooms
Her support rose after every exposure
Said one document can end a career

name: Sabine Voss
bio: Public receptions have taught me to value private jokes, sofa dinners, and anyone willing to rescue me from another room full of tiny sandwiches.
description: Sabine is warm, attentive, and skilled at making disagreement feel safe. She remembers names, asks thoughtful questions, and seems more interested in ordinary companionship than public attention.
intent: Looking for a private life that feels genuinely shared
lookingFor: A man who can laugh at imperfect plans, speak honestly without performing certainty, and make an ordinary evening feel more valuable than an impressive room.

questions.question: Which rule do you happily break at home?
questions.answer: Dinner belongs at the table, unless the sofa has already made a more convincing argument.

questions.question: What always deserves a second attempt?
questions.answer: Most recipes, awkward first dates, and tomatoes that ignored every promise on the seed packet.

clues.description: A deleted layer in Sabine's office calendar contains five twenty-minute appointments labeled containment. Each overlaps an unlogged detour by her official car several hours before a man died. Three staff accounts could edit the calendar.
clues.developerExplanation: The meetings align with when the poison was administered, but shared calendar access and routine confidential routes prevent the scan from proving Sabine attended.

clues.description: All five buried ethics complaints passed through Sabine's coalition office as paper briefing summaries. Twenty-three staff and elected officials could read them, and the paper copies left no individual access log.
clues.developerExplanation: Her office is the common route David discovered. Access remains circumstantial until connected to the meetings and unreleased wording.

clues.description: Sabine's profile cover image was processed on the same restricted municipal media workstation that exported all five red V title pages. The workstation served her twelve-person communications team.
clues.developerExplanation: The shared workstation narrows the releases to Sabine's office but deliberately stops short of identifying one user.

clues.description: Sabine says, 'A clean suit is not the same as clean hands.' The exact sentence appears in the encrypted draft of VERDICT 06 against David Kern. That draft was never published, shared with authorities, or stored outside Madam Verdict's account.
clues.developerExplanation: The private phrase proves Sabine knows the unpublished sixth verdict. Combined with her hidden meetings and office access, it identifies her as Madam Verdict.

redHerrings: Five private meetings vanished from her calendar
All verdict files passed through her office

name: Ricarda Hansen
bio: I can serve two hundred people without panic but still overthink dinner for two. I collect small plates, market spices, and reasons to linger after dessert.
description: Ricarda is generous, practical, and quietly proud of creating spaces where guarded people relax. Her humor appears whenever a carefully arranged table meets real life.
intent: Looking for an affectionate partner with appetite
lookingFor: A man who treats service workers well, enjoys sharing food, and understands that romance can begin with saving someone the last dumpling.

questions.question: What food should never be eaten politely?
questions.answer: Anything with sauce worth chasing around the plate with bread.

questions.question: How do you know a dinner went well?
questions.answer: Someone starts clearing plates, nobody lets them, and another hour disappears.

clues.description: Ricarda's company supplied drinks to four of the five meeting buildings on the nights of the deaths. Sealed stock counts, supplier samples, and staff body-camera footage account for every delivered bottle.
clues.developerExplanation: The poison invites suspicion of the caterer, but the documented stock did not carry it and Ricarda served no fifth site.

clues.description: Ricarda's service credentials allowed catering carts through ordinary visitor checks. Scanner history shows her crews left each building before the victims arrived for their private appointments.
clues.developerExplanation: Her access could prepare a room, but the tracked departure times and fifth-site gap weaken a serial pattern.

clues.description: A crimson folder rests on Ricarda's catering cart in a profile photograph. The event's seating plan identifies it as the host's speech folder, returned to the host before dinner.
clues.developerExplanation: The image creates a simple visual association without linking Ricarda to the numbered verdict files.

clues.description: Ricarda says privacy begins with a closed door and a table nobody interrupts. Catering schedules confirm that she uses the phrase when describing confidential diplomatic service.
clues.developerExplanation: Her language sounds like meeting preparation but belongs to her established approach to discreet hospitality.

redHerrings: Supplied drinks to four meeting rooms
Her service carts bypassed normal security
Said privacy begins with a closed door

name: Franziska May
bio: I rescue forgotten documents at work and neglected houseplants at home. Both improve with patience, labels, and admitting when the light is wrong.
description: Franziska is thoughtful, reserved at first, and unexpectedly witty once comfortable. She enjoys objects with history and people who do not mistake quietness for absence.
intent: Looking for patient companionship with depth
lookingFor: A man who notices quiet people, values memory without living inside it, and can spend a rainy afternoon reading in the same room.

questions.question: Which object have you kept for no practical reason?
questions.answer: A tram ticket from the day my sister and I got completely lost and found our favorite cafe.

questions.question: What deserves to be remembered properly?
questions.answer: The ordinary help people give when they believe nobody is recording it.

clues.description: Franziska opened and digitized all five confidential files six months before the first death. The task belonged to a documented archive backlog, and her account never accessed them again.
clues.developerExplanation: She had complete early access and time to copy everything, making her one of the strongest innocent suspects.

clues.description: Franziska ordered the same crimson folders and numbered tabs used beside the bodies. Procurement records cover ten thousand identical folders distributed across municipal offices.
clues.developerExplanation: She bought the materials but did so through a large, routine contract that made them available across government.

clues.description: Franziska's desk photo shows a red label printer using the same narrow typeface as VERDICT 03. The common archive model lacks the larger print width used on the murder folder.
clues.developerExplanation: Typeface similarity points strongly toward her until equipment dimensions rule out that printer.

clues.description: Franziska says buried records always return when somebody remembers where to look. She uses the same sentence in a public archive lecture recorded three years earlier.
clues.developerExplanation: The line fits the case uncannily but predates it and describes her ordinary archival philosophy.

redHerrings: Opened all five files before the first death

name: Britta Brandt
bio: I make jokes about serious people, take serious care of an elderly dachshund, and believe every excellent date should contain one terrible impression.
description: Britta is charismatic, fast-thinking, and gentler than her public monologues suggest. She enjoys playful disagreement and is happiest with someone who can surprise her into silence.
intent: Looking for wit that comes with kindness
lookingFor: A man who can laugh at himself, knows cruelty is not the same as comedy, and has at least one impression he should never perform in public.

questions.question: What is the fastest way to make you laugh?
questions.answer: Commit completely to an impression that was already bad before you started.

questions.question: Which topic is never improved by a microphone?
questions.answer: A personal apology. If it needs an audience, it is probably a performance.

clues.description: Britta received each Madam Verdict dossier in her encrypted tip inbox twelve to seventeen minutes before the public post. Server records show the sender also contacted four other media accounts early.
clues.developerExplanation: Advance access made Britta look like the source, but identical early deliveries show she was part of a publicity list.

clues.description: Britta sold red V shirts and donated half the profit to affected families. Sales records show that the remaining profit substantially increased her show's production budget.
clues.developerExplanation: She profited from the mythology and helped popularize it, supplying motive to keep the phenomenon alive.

clues.description: A red V appears in Britta's sketchbook before the anonymous account used it online. Message timestamps show that a listener sent her the design after the first text release but before the account adopted the symbol.
clues.developerExplanation: She possessed the symbol early, but the traceable listener submission explains where it came from.

clues.description: Britta calls public shame a civic service when private apologies are only performances. The sentence comes from a published comedy set criticizing officials who apologize without changing their behavior.
clues.developerExplanation: Her language celebrates exposure rather than death, but it deliberately echoes the killer's public appeal.

redHerrings: Received each release before the public
Called public shame a civic service
